pages.title: Sending marketing and transactional emails to your partners
pages.description: Learn how to craft and send marketing and transactional emails to your partners to increase partner engagement and drive conversions.
pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Advanced plans and
  above.

On RevRoute, you can send marketing and transactional emails to your partners to boost partner engagement and increase conversions.

In this guide, we'll learn how to set up your email domain on RevRoute and start sending emails to your partners. Without a verified domain, you can't fill in the **From** field in the campaign editor, so start there.

**Справка.**

  Sending partner emails with your own domain (e.g. `partners.acme.com`) is not
  only good for branding but will also drastically improve deliverability and
  help avoid the dreaded spam folder.

## Email domain setup

Email domains are connected in your workspace settings: **Settings** → **Domains**, **Email domains** tab — app.revroute.ru/settings/domains/email.

Click **Add domain** and enter the domain you want to send emails from. We recommend using a subdomain (e.g. `partners.acme.com`) to improve trust and deliverability. Specific "from" addresses are set later, when you create a campaign.

Once the domain is added, RevRoute shows the DNS records to create with your domain's DNS provider, along with the verification status of each one. A separate **DMARC (Recommended)** block contains a recommended `_dmarc` TXT record — we strongly recommend adding it to help prevent email spoofing.

When all records are verified, the domain status changes to **Verified**, and you're ready to send partner emails.

Until the domain is verified, you can prepare campaigns as drafts, but the **From** field in the editor stays unavailable, so you can't send or schedule a campaign.

### Warming up your email domain

“Warming up” your domain means gradually increasing your email-sending volume to build trust and improve deliverability. The goal is to send consistently without sudden spikes that might look suspicious to inbox providers.

Any time you start using a new domain or expect a large increase in sending volume, you should warm up your domain. A thoughtful warm-up plan helps prevent greylisting, throttling, and spam filtering, while building a solid sender reputation.

Keep an eye on your bounce rate — the **Bounced** metric in the Metrics panel. It should stay below **4%**. If it rises above that, slow down your sending and review the cause.

Example warm-up plan:

1. Add your custom domain and start sending **transactional** emails to warm it up.
2. After 2–3 days, send a small **marketing** campaign to your smallest group (e.g., “VIP Group”), then a slightly larger one (“Silver Group”).
3. Once your domain is fully warmed up, you can send marketing campaigns regularly to all groups (e.g., “Default Group”).

## Where to find email campaigns

In your program menu, open **Email Campaigns** under **Engagement**. At the top of the page are the **All**, **Marketing**, and **Transactional** counters — click one to filter the list. Below are a filter by status and type, a search by name, and the campaigns table with each campaign's status and creation date.

| Status    | What it means                                                                   |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Draft     | The campaign hasn't been sent or published yet                                  |
| Scheduled | The marketing email will go out at the selected date and time                   |
| Sending   | The marketing email is being sent to partners — sending happens in batches      |
| Sent      | The marketing email has been sent                                               |
| Canceled  | The marketing email was canceled before or during sending                       |
| Active    | The transactional email is published and goes out as soon as a partner meets the condition |
| Paused    | The transactional email is paused and isn't sent to new recipients              |

## Creating a new campaign

Click **Create campaign** in the top-right corner and select the type of email you want to send: **Marketing** or **Transactional**. RevRoute creates a draft and opens the editor.

### Marketing

Marketing emails are one-off messages you send manually. They're great for announcements, product updates, and promotions.

**Examples:**

- “Introducing our newest feature”
- “Black Friday / Cyber Monday promotion”
- “Check out our latest blog post or promo video”

### Transactional

Transactional emails are automated messages triggered by specific partner actions — like joining your program, reaching a milestone, or staying enrolled for a certain period.

**Examples:**

- “Welcome to the program! Here’s how to start earning.”
- “Congrats on your first conversion — here’s how to reach your next 10.”
- “You’ve crossed 100,000 ₽ in commissions! You’re now among our top earners.”

## Email builder

Both Marketing and Transactional emails include:

- **Name** — the internal name of your campaign;
- **From** — the sender address: you enter the mailbox name, and the domain is filled in from your verified email domain;
- **To** — partner groups: **All groups** by default, or click **Edit** to choose specific ones;
- **Subject** — the subject line of the email;
- **Preview** — the short text shown next to or below the subject line in the recipient’s inbox; add the row using the **Preview text** button to the right of the subject;
- the email body — below the formatting toolbar, up to the “End of email” marker.

Drafts are saved automatically as you type. When you edit a scheduled or paused campaign, an **Unsaved changes** bar appears at the bottom with **Save changes** and **Discard** buttons.

### Marketing fields

In the **When** field, pick the send date and time from the calendar, or type them in words — e.g. “in 2 hours”. This is helpful when planning email campaigns for the future.

The button in the top-right corner reads **Send** — or **Schedule** if the selected date is in the future. Before sending, RevRoute shows how many partners will receive the email and asks you to confirm. Until all required fields are filled in, the button is disabled, and its tooltip explains what's missing.

To cancel a scheduled campaign, click **Cancel** — the email won't go out at the scheduled time. You can also cancel a campaign that's already sending, but emails go out in batches, so a few more may be sent before it stops. Canceling can't be undone.

### Transactional fields

Instead of a date, transactional campaigns have a **Logic** field — the condition that triggers the email. For example: “When partner joins the program” or “When partner's total leads reaches at least 10”.

For every condition except joining the program, a threshold appears next to it — a number, an amount, or, for enrollment duration, a period from the list.

| Condition           | When the email is sent                                         |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Joins the program   | A partner enrolls in your program                              |
| Total leads         | A partner reaches a specific number of leads                   |
| Total conversions   | A partner reaches a specific number of conversions             |
| Total revenue       | A partner's revenue reaches a specific amount                  |
| Total commissions   | A partner's commissions reach a specific amount                |
| Enrollment duration | A partner has been enrolled for 1, 3, 7, 14, or 30 days        |

To launch the campaign, click **Publish** and confirm: as soon as a partner from the selected groups meets the condition, they receive the email. You can **Pause** an active campaign and **Resume** it later. While a campaign is active, its recipients and logic can't be changed — pause it first.

### Formatting

Above the email body is the formatting toolbar: bold, italic, strikethrough, H1 and H2 headings, link, partner variable, and image.

The `@` button inserts a partner variable — `PartnerName` or `PartnerEmail`. In the editor it shows as `{{PartnerName}}`, and each partner sees their own details in the email.

You can also use Markdown-style syntax for bold text, italics, and headings: `**bold text**`, `*italic*`, `# ` or `## ` at the start of a line.

## Email previews

Before launching a campaign, you can send a test version to yourself or teammates for review. Click **⋮** in the top-right corner of the editor and select **Send preview**. In the **Send preview email** dialog, enter the email addresses separated by commas. You can send a preview once the campaign has a subject and a body.

From the same menu, you can **Duplicate** the campaign — the copy opens in the editor — or **Delete** it. To delete, type `confirm delete campaign`.

## Campaign metrics

Once a marketing campaign has been sent or a transactional one has been published, the **Metrics** panel opens on the right side of the editor, showing how many emails were **Delivered**, **Opened**, and **Bounced**. Below is a list of events by partner with a search by name or email, so you can see which partners opened the email.

## Partner replies

When a partner replies to any email you send through RevRoute, their reply goes to your program's support email address. You can view or update that address on your Resources page, in the **Help and support** section.

This means that even if you change your sending domain later, all partner replies will continue to arrive in the same inbox.

pages.title: Messaging your partners
pages.description: Learn how to use the messaging center to communicate with your partners in real time, with email notifications and read statuses built in.
pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Advanced plans and
  above.

On RevRoute, you can use the messaging center to communicate directly with the partners in your program. Partners get notified about new messages via email and reply to you from their partner dashboard.

## Messages location

In your program menu, open **Messages** to see all your conversations with partners and compose new messages.

## Messages overview

The messaging center has three panels:

| Panel        | Content                                         |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Messages     | All your conversations in one place.            |
| Conversation | The full thread with your selected partner.     |
| Profile      | Key info and performance stats for the partner. |

### Conversation list

The left panel lists every conversation with your partners: the partner's name and profile image, plus the date and an excerpt of the latest message. Select a conversation to pick up where you left off, or click the **Pencil** button in the top right of the panel to compose a new message — it opens a search for partners in your program.

### Conversation panel

The center panel shows the full thread with your partner. Your workspace teammates can message partners too if their role allows it, with their profile images shown beside each message.

Type your message in the field at the bottom of the panel and click **Send**. The field also has emoji, bold, italic, and link buttons.

### Message status

Each message sent has a check mark:

- **Single check mark** – delivered
- **Double check marks** – delivered and read (either in the notification email or in the partner dashboard)

### Profile panel

The right panel shows the partner's status in your program, their email, group, and performance stats: clicks, leads, conversions, revenue, commissions, and net revenue. Click **Change group** to move the partner to another group, or **View profile** to open their full profile. You can hide the panel with the button in the top-right corner of the conversation.

## Message notifications

RevRoute notifies you about new partner messages via email. You can turn the **New message from partner** notification on or off in **Settings** → **Notifications**, under **Partner program**.

## Disabling messaging

If you prefer to handle support outside RevRoute, you can disable partner messaging.

Go to your program's **Resources**, turn off the **Messages** switch in the **Help and support** section, and click **Save**.

When messaging is disabled, partners see a notice in their dashboard that your program uses external support, with a button to email the support address specified in that section. Your **Messages** page shows that messaging is disabled, with a button to go to **Resources** and turn it back on.

pages.title: Program bounties
pages.description: Drive partner engagement by creating performance and submission bounties for your partner program
pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

Bounties let you reward partners for hitting goals or completing work — for example, a video review of your product or a blog post. This guide covers how to create bounties, set their criteria, and review partner submissions.

Bounties live in your program menu: the **Bounties** section under **Engagement**. Partners see the bounties available to them in their partner dashboard.

On the **Bounties** page, each bounty is a card showing its name, dates, reward, how many partners have already completed it or submitted work, and the groups it's available to. If the reward is a custom amount, the card shows the reward description instead.

## Creating a bounty

Click **Create bounty** (or press `C`) to open the **Create bounty** sheet. First, choose the type:

- **Performance** — a reward for reaching goals: leads, conversions, revenue, or commissions;
- **Submission** — a reward for completing a task, such as a post or an event.

The **Details** block includes, for both types:

| Field                  | Description                                                                                     |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Start date             | Turn on the switch to launch the bounty later. Without it, the bounty starts right after creation |
| End date               | The bounty ends after this date. It must be at least one hour after the start date             |
| Description (optional) | Requirements for completing the bounty, up to 5,000 characters                                  |

In the **Groups** block, choose who can access the bounty: **All groups**, or **Select groups** and check the partner groups you need.

Click **Create bounty** and confirm in the **Confirm bounty creation** dialog, which previews the bounty card. On Advanced plans and above, the **Send notification to …** checkbox in this dialog is on: RevRoute will email partners in the selected groups about the new bounty. If you don't want to send the email, clear the checkbox before confirming.

## Performance bounties

Performance bounties reward partners for measurable results: the number of leads or conversions, revenue, or commissions. Completion is tracked automatically and doesn't need approval.

Examples:

- Drive 500 leads and earn an extra 100,000 ₽ bonus
- Generate 100,000 ₽ in revenue and earn an extra 25,000 ₽ bonus
- Earn 500,000 ₽ in commissions and get an extra 50,000 ₽ bonus

Set the condition in the **Criteria** block: “When a partner's [new or lifetime] [leads, conversions, revenue, or commissions] reach at least [value]”, followed by “Then pay [amount]”. For revenue and commissions, the threshold is an amount in rubles. The name of a performance bounty is generated automatically from its condition and reward.

- **New** — only results earned after the bounty starts count. For example, if the bounty rewards 10 leads, every partner must drive 10 new leads after launch, regardless of how many leads they had before.
- **Lifetime** — results across the partner's entire time in your program count. A partner who already has 10 leads qualifies for the reward right away.

## Submission bounties

Submission bounties reward partners for actions that need review, such as a social media post, a blog article, or an event. The partner submits their work, and the reward is paid once you approve it.

Examples:

- Publish a YouTube video to raise awareness
- Write a blog post about your product
- Host an event (in person or online) to promote your brand

Submission bounties have two more fields in the **Details** block:

| Field             | Description                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Name              | The bounty name partners see. Required, up to 100 characters                                                                           |
| Submission window | Partners can submit only during the last 2–14 days before the end date. The switch is available once an end date is set               |

How partners prove completion is set in the **Criteria** block on one of two tabs: **Manual submission** or **Social metrics**.

### Manual submission

By default, partners describe how they completed the bounty in a text field. You can also turn on:

- **Require at least one image** — and limit the number of images (4 by default);
- **Require at least one URL** — and limit the number of URLs (10 by default). In **Allowed domains**, you can list the domains the URLs must come from — for example, only your social accounts or blog. Enter a domain and click **Add**, then add the next one. Subdomains of the listed domains are accepted too.

Below, set the reward: **On approval, pay** a **flat amount** or a **custom amount**. A flat amount is the same for every submission. A custom amount is set when you approve each submission — for example, if you pay for an event based on its size. In that case, describe the reward for partners: the description appears on the bounty card instead of an amount, for example “5,000–15,000 ₽ depending on attendance”.

### Social metrics

The **Social metrics** tab is for bounties where the reward depends on how a post performs. The condition reads: “If a post on [channel] gets at least [value] [metric]”, followed by “Then pay [amount]”. Channels: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, and X/Twitter; metrics: views or likes.

The **Add variable bonus** button adds a variable bonus: on top of the base reward, partners earn an extra amount for each additional increment, up to a cap. For example, an extra 500 ₽ for every 100 views, up to 1,000 views.

RevRoute updates post metrics on its own. The bounty page shows when they were last synced, and the **Refresh stats** button starts a sync manually.

**Совет.**

  Social metrics bounties are only available on Advanced plans and
  above.

## Reviewing submissions

Submissions for submission bounties need to be reviewed before you approve or reject them. Open the bounty in the **Bounties** section: the top of the page shows the bounty terms and how many partners have submitted, and below is the submissions table with a filter. The table shows the partner, their group, the submission status, the submission and review dates, and progress. Submission statuses: **Draft**, **Submitted**, **Approved**, **Rejected**.

To open a submission, click its row or choose **Review submission** in the row menu. The **Review submission** sheet shows the partner info, the submission details, and the proof provided, along with the **Approve** and **Reject** buttons.

RevRoute notifies you about new submissions via email: turn on the **New bounty submission** notification in **Settings** → **Notifications**.

### Approving submissions

Once you approve a submission, RevRoute creates a commission that is included in the partner's next payout.

**Справка.**

  If the bounty uses a **custom amount**, you'll need to enter the reward for
  this partner in the **Reward** field when approving.

### Rejecting submissions

When rejecting a submission, choose a reason and add a note if needed:

- Invalid proof
- Duplicate submission
- Out of time window
- Did not meet criteria
- Other

No commission is created for a rejected submission. From the row menu, you can **Reopen** a submission — it goes back to draft so the partner can rework it.

To edit or delete a bounty, use the **⋮** menu in the top-right corner of the bounty page: **Edit bounty** or **Delete bounty**. A bounty that already has submissions can't be deleted.

pages.title: Offering dual-sided incentives
pages.description: How to give your partners a discount for their customers: a group discount, a partner promo code, resolving the code on your side, and the commission for a sale made with the code.
pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

A dual-sided incentive rewards both sides: the partner earns a reward for the customer they referred, and the customer gets a discount for coming in through the partner's link or promo code.

Some examples include:

- 25% discount for the first 12 months
- 30% lifetime discount
- ₽5,000 one-off discount
- A bonus in units of your product — e.g. 100 extra leads credited to the balance

This drives word-of-mouth growth: partners are more likely to share their link if it gives their audience a discount, and the audience is more likely to click if a special deal is waiting for them.

## How it works

RevRoute stores the discount terms and knows which partner each promo code belongs to. No money passes through RevRoute: the discount itself is applied by your payment system — card acquiring, your own billing, an invoice, whatever you use. You don't need to create coupons in your payment system.

The whole chain:

1. **You create a discount** for a partner group: a percentage, a fixed amount or a bonus, plus its duration.
2. **The partner gets a promo code** tied to their referral link — you create it manually in the partner's profile or turn on automatic creation. The partner sees the code in their dashboard and shares it with their audience.
3. **A customer comes to you** through the partner's link or types the promo code at checkout. Your site or server asks RevRoute whose code it is and what the terms are, and applies the discount.
4. **After payment you send the sale** to RevRoute — the partner earns a commission according to their group's rules.

Steps 1 and 2 happen in the UI, no developer needed. Steps 3 and 4 are an integration on your side: two API requests.

**Create a discount for a partner group**

Open the partner group that should get the discount, go to the **Discounts** tab and click **Create**. A group can have only one discount; if different partners need different terms, set up separate groups.

In the **Create discount** sheet, pick the offer type:

- **Discount** — a percentage or a fixed amount off the payment. Set the amount and the duration: **one time** (first payment only), **for several months** or **lifetime**.
- **Bonus** — an offer in units of your product that your system credits, e.g. "100 leads credited to the balance". Set the **Quantity**, **Unit** and **Description** — partners and customers will see the description.

The **Automatically create promo codes** toggle turns on automatic code creation for the group's partners — see the next step. The **To** block shows which partners in the group get the discount. Confirm with **Create discount**.

**Внимание.**

  The amount, type and duration of a discount can't be changed after creation
  — only the description, the bonus terms and automatic code creation. To
  change the terms, delete the discount and create a new one. Deleting a
  discount also deletes the promo codes of the partners in that group.

**Give the partner a promo code**

A promo code is what the partner gives their audience where a link can't be placed: in a podcast, a video, a post. Each code is tied to one of the partner's referral links, and a link can have only one code. Sales made with the code count towards the same link as clicks on it.

**Automatically.** If the **Automatically create promo codes** toggle is on in the discount sheet, RevRoute creates a code for the default link of every active partner in the group, and for new partners when their application is approved. The code is built from the first word of the partner's name in capitals plus the discount amount: `IVAN20OFF` for 20%, `IVAN5000OFF` for ₽5,000. If that code is already taken in the program, a short suffix is appended.

**Manually.** Open the partner's profile, the **Links** tab, and click **Create code** in the **Promo codes** block. If the button is disabled, hover over it to see why: either the partner's group has no discount, or all of the partner's links already have promo codes. In the latter case, create a new link for the partner first.

**Create code** opens the **New discount code** dialog. Pick the link to tie the code to under **Referral link**, enter the code in **Discount code** — the field hint shows the partner's name in capitals; leave the field empty to have the code built automatically — and click **Create discount code**. The code is stored in capitals and copied to your clipboard right away.

**Внимание.**

  Promo codes cannot be edited after creation — only deleted. Double-check the
  code and the link before creating it.

Once created, the code appears in the **Promo codes** block next to its link. The partner sees it in their dashboard on that link's card, labelled **Promo code** — clicking it copies the code. The discount terms are shown to the partner in the program's reward description: "New users get 10% off for 6 months".

**Apply the discount on your side**

A customer can reach you in two ways, and for each of them RevRoute returns the partner and their discount terms.

**The customer clicked the partner's link.** If the RevRoute script is installed on your site, the partner and the discount are already available in `window.RevRouteAnalytics` and in the `rr_partner_data` cookie — see Displaying a discount banner below. On the server, the same data can be fetched by the value of the `rr_id` cookie: `GET /discount-codes/resolve?clickId=<rr_id>`.

**The customer typed a promo code at checkout.** Ask RevRoute whose code it is. From your server, call `GET /discount-codes/resolve` with your workspace API key:

[пример кода: bash]

[пример кода: js]

The response (internal fields omitted):

[пример кода: json]

How to read the terms:

- `offerType` — `discount` or `bonus` (a bonus in units: `bonusQuantity`, `bonusUnit`, `description`).
- `type` — `percentage` or `flat` (fixed amount). For `flat`, `amount` is **in kopecks**: `500000` means ₽5,000.
- `maxDuration` — the duration in months: `0` means the first payment only, `null` means lifetime.
- `discount: null` — the code has no discount (it was deleted), there is nothing to apply.

An unknown code returns `404`: no such promo code exists in the program, so no discount should be given.

Straight from the checkout page, without an API key, a code can be resolved with `POST /track/discount-code` — it returns the partner and the terms, but without the partner's email or the program's internal data:

[пример кода: js]

`domain` is the referral link domain of your program. Only the sites listed under **Allowed hostnames** in **Settings → Analytics** may call this endpoint; while the list is empty it responds with `403` — this protects codes from being enumerated. The limit is 20 requests per minute per IP address.

From here on, applying the discount is up to you: reduce the invoice amount, add a coupon in your payment system, credit bonus units — whatever fits your system.

**Send the sale — the partner earns a commission**

An applied discount doesn't earn the partner a commission by itself: RevRoute only learns about the sale from your request. After payment, send it to `POST /track/sale` and, if the customer came in without clicking a link, pass the promo code in the `discountCode` field:

[пример кода: bash]

[пример кода: js]

How RevRoute decides who gets credit for the sale:

- If `clickId` is passed (the value of the `rr_id` cookie), the sale goes to the partner whose link was clicked — `discountCode` is ignored.
- If a customer with this `customerExternalId` is already known (for example, you sent their sign-up to `/track/lead`), the sale is attributed to them as usual.
- Otherwise the sale goes to the partner who owns the `discountCode`. An unknown code returns `404` and the sale is not recorded.

`POST /track/lead` accepts the `discountCode` field too — for the case where a customer signs up with a promo code before paying. Pass the amount the customer actually paid in `amount` — the partner's commission is calculated from it.

## Displaying a discount banner

Once dual-sided incentives are set up, the next step is to show the discount right on your pricing page or landing page: "Ivan referred you to Acme and gave you 20% off".

All you need is the RevRoute script with client-side click tracking enabled: when a visitor lands on your site via a valid referral link, the script fetches the partner and discount data for you.

The script stores the partner and discount data in the `rr_partner_data` cookie as
a JSON object:

[пример кода: json]

The `discount` fields are the same as in the `/discount-codes/resolve` response above; `code` is the partner's promo code for this link, if one exists — you can show it to the customer.

In page code the same data is available on `window.RevRouteAnalytics`. Read it
inside the `ready` callback — by then the script has fetched the click data.

[пример кода: html]

**Внимание.**

  `partner.name` and `partner.image` are URL-encoded inside the cookie — run
  them through `decodeURIComponent` before rendering.

pages.title: Managing your program partners
pages.description: Understand how all your partners are performing and contributing to the success of your partner program.

headings.text: Where to find your program partners

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

## Where to find your program partners

In the **Partner Program** menu, click **All Partners** to see everyone in your program.

## Inviting partners

On the **Partners** page, click **Invite partner** to open the invite panel.

Learn more about inviting partners here.

## Importing partners

Click the `⋮` menu to import partners from supported platforms into your RevRoute program.

RevRoute currently supports importing from:

- Rewardful
- Tolt
- PartnerStack
- FirstPromoter

If you’d like to import from other platforms, let us know.

## Exporting partners

Click the `⋮` menu and choose **Export as CSV** to download your partner data for use anywhere.

## Partner table

The partner table gives you a complete view of everyone in your program. By default, partners are sorted by **net revenue**, starting with your highest performers. This makes it easy to see who is driving the most value at a glance.

You can sort the table by any column header. For example, select **Conversions** to sort partners by the number of conversions instead of revenue.

### Default columns

When you first open the table, you will see a focused set of columns designed to give you a quick read on partner performance.

| Column      | Description                                               |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| Group       | The group this partner is in                              |
| Location    | The partner's declared location                           |
| Clicks      | Total number of clicks on the partner's links             |
| Leads       | Total number of leads generated by the partner's links    |
| Conversions | Total number of leads that converted to paying customers  |
| Revenue     | Total revenue generated by the partner's links            |
| Commissions | Total commissions paid to the partner for their referrals |
| Net Revenue | Net revenue after commissions                             |

These can be changed anytime by clicking the `Gear icon` in the top right of the table, allowing you to enable or disable additional columns.

### Additional columns

If you need a deeper view, you can turn on extra performance and attribution metrics. These optional columns help you understand partner quality, funnel efficiency, and long term value more clearly.

| Column        | Description                                           | Equation                          |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| EPC           | Earnings Per Click                                    | Total Revenue ÷ Total Clicks      |
| Avg LTV       | Average lifetime value for each paying customer       | Total Revenue ÷ Total Conversions |
| Click -> Lead | Percentage of clicks that become leads                | Total Leads ÷ Total Clicks        |
| Click -> Conv | Percentage of clicks that convert to paying customers | Total Conversions ÷ Total Clicks  |
| Lead -> Conv  | Percentage of leads that convert to paying customers  | Total Conversions ÷ Total Leads   |
| ROAS          | Return On Ad Spend                                    | Total Revenue ÷ Total Commissions |

### Filter and search

Use filters to sort partners by group, status, or location. Filters help you spot top-performing partners.

You can also use the search field to search by name, email, or link. This is helpful when looking for a specific partner.

**Status filter**

Filter by status to see who’s active and who isn’t.

| Status      | Description                                                                                                                                                            |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Approved    | Partner has joined and can earn rewards                                                                                                                                |
| Invited     | Partners that have been invited to your program but haven't accepted the invite yet                                                                                    |
| Declined    | Partners that have declined your invitation to join                                                                                                                    |
| Archived    | Partner has been removed from the program                                                                                                                              |
| Banned      | Partners that you have banned from your program                                                                                                                        |
| Deactivated | Partners that you've deactivated your partnership with. This could be used for ending a partnership for non abuse-related reasons (e.g. commercial/financial reasons). |

### More dropdown

For each partner, click the ⋯ menu to see more controls.

These additional controls include:

- **Approved partners**: View commissions, Archive partner, and Ban Partner
  Archive partner, and Ban Partner
- **Invited partners**: Resend invite and
  Delete invite
- **Archived partners**: View commissions, Unarchive partner, and
  Ban partner.
- **Banned partners**: View commissions, Archive partner, and
  Unban partner.

## Partner details

Click on a partner’s row to see their details, like their profile, performance, short links, payouts, and commissions.

### Links

To see all referral links for this partner, click **Links**. You'll also see partner discount codes if they have been added. Learn more about partner discount codes.

If you need to create a link for your partner, click **Create link**.

### Payouts

Click **Payouts** to see all payouts for a partner. Click any payout row to view its details.

### Profile

To view the partner's profile details, click the **Profile** button next to their name in the right column.

This will open a panel where you can view details like their country, bio, and connected websites or social accounts. You'll also be able to view the partner's original application response when they first applied.

### Comments

Click **Comments** to view and add comments for this partner, which only your workspace can view. You can also edit and delete your own comments in case a mistake was made.

### Commissions

Click **Commissions** to open a page showing commissions filtered for this partner. Learn more about partner commissions here.

### Manual commission

Occasionally, you might need to create a one-off or recurring commission to account for a missed commission or other reasons. On RevRoute, you can easily create those commissions via the dashboard, and they will be included in the next payout for that partner.

Click **Create commission** to get started. Learn more about manual commissions here.

## Advanced settings

**Внимание.**

  Use caution when changing any of the advanced partner settings.

To access your partner's advanced settings, from their profile page, click the `⋮` dropdown and select **Advanced settings**.

### Tenant ID

If you need to update the partner's tenant ID, changing the ID here will update the tenantId for all their links as well. This could potentially impact any custom integration you have set up, so only change if you’re certain the information is correct and necessary.

### Customer data sharing

Enabling this setting allows this partner to see customer data on any leads or sales the partner has made.

Instead of the hidden email addresses, they will see the full customer email address and their name. They'll also be able to click through the customer to view the sales history.

pages.title: Managing your partners with groups
pages.description: Learn how you can create partner groups to segment partners by rewards, discounts, performance, location, and more.

headings.text: What types of partner groups can I create?
Where can I view my partner groups?
What is the default partner group?
Adding multiple partners to a group
How many partner groups can I create?

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

Partner groups help you organize your program so it runs more efficiently. You can segment partners by rewards, discounts, performance, location, and more, making it easier to tailor incentives and track results.

## What types of partner groups can I create?

Here are some examples of partner groups you can create on RevRoute:

**By persona**

- **Agencies** – Marketing or creative agencies promoting your product for their clients.
- **Content creators** – Bloggers, podcasters, or YouTubers producing relevant content.
- **Media publishers** – Websites, magazines, or networks with aligned audiences.

**By vertical**

- **Students** – University clubs, campus ambassadors, or student-led initiatives.
- **Finance** – Partners in banking, fintech, or investment sectors.
- **Tech** – Developers, SaaS providers, or technology-focused communities.

**By performance tier**

- **Rising stars** – New partners showing strong growth potential.
- **Top performers** – Consistently exceeding sales or referral targets.
- **Elite partners** – Highest earners driving significant revenue and strategic wins.

## Where can I view my partner groups?

In your partner program menu, open **Partners** → **Groups**. The table shows how many partners each group has and the clicks, leads, conversions, revenue, and commissions they drive.

## What is the default partner group?

Your program always has a group labelled **Default** — in the screenshot above it's "Интеграторы". It can be renamed at any time.

**Справка.**

  You cannot delete your default partner group. This group will also be the
  group that your partners will be reassigned to whenever you delete another
  partner group.

## Creating a group

To create a group, click **Create group** in the top right corner or press `C` on your keyboard.

| Field          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Group name     | Add a name to your group to help easily identify it later. Pick the group color with the dot on the right of the field.   **This name is for internal use only and is never visible to your partners.**                                                      |
| URL identifier | Filled in automatically from the name. Each partner group uses a unique application landing page, which you can share with partners you want to automatically add to that group when they apply.   **Anyone you share the application link with can see it.** |

Once the group is created, its non-editable **Group ID** appears in the group settings — you'll use it to embed the RevRoute referral dashboard in your app.

## Group rewards

Every partner group can have one of each of the following:

| Reward type                 | Description                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Click-based (pay-per-click) | Rewarding partners for driving clicks to your product – similar to how Google Ads' pay-per-click works.                                            |
| Lead-based (pay-per-lead)   | A more effective alternative to pay-per-click, where you reward partners for leads generated (e.g. demo requests, free trial signups, etc.)        |
| Sale-based (pay-per-sale)   | This is the most common reward type, where you reward partners for driving sales to your product either via a rev-share or fixed-price commission. |

Rewards live on the group page's **Rewards** tab.

To create a reward, click **Create** on any of the reward types. Learn more about creating rewards here.

If you want to reuse a reward from your default group, click **Duplicate from default group** to copy over the parameters and save time.

## Group discounts

You can also create dual-sided incentives for your affiliate/referral programs, which give special discounts to customers who sign up via a referral link.
Some examples include:

- 25% discount for the first 12 months
- 30% lifetime discount
- ₽5,000 one-off discount

This can drive powerful word-of-mouth growth as partners are more likely to share their link if it gives their audience/user base additional discounts, and on the other hand, their users are more likely to click on their links as well if they're getting a special deal.

You can create only one discount per group. To create a discount, open the group page's **Discounts** tab and click **Create**.

Learn more about creating discounts here.

## Group settings

Each group has individual settings on the group page's **Settings** tab.

### Group name

The name of the partner group can be changed at any time. It's for internal use only and is never visible to your partners.

### Group slug

This is the same URL identifier you set when creating the group. By default, it auto-generates from the group name, but you're able to change this at any time. For program landing pages and internal group page URLs.

**Совет.**
The default group slug cannot be changed — the default group doesn't have this field.

### Group ID

When setting up the RevRoute embedded referral dashboard, you'll use this group ID. The ID cannot be changed.

### Payout holding period

Specify how long your commissions will be held in "pending" status before becoming eligible for payout: 0, 7, 14, 30 (recommended), 60, or 90 days. Learn more.

### Auto-approve

Enable or disable auto-approving new applicants to this group. Learn more.

### Group move rules

Automatically move partners into this group when they meet specific criteria. This is useful when you want partners to earn higher rewards as they progress in your program, without needing to manage groups manually.

To set up a rule, click **Add rule**, pick a metric in the **If partner** row — the **Move partner to** row already points to the current group — and click **Save changes**.

You can move partners based on performance metrics like total leads, conversions, revenue, or commissions. Multiple rules can be combined so only partners who meet your exact requirements are moved into the group.

**Example:** Move partners to the `VIP` group once their total commissions reach ₽10,000.

**Совет.**

  Group move rules are only available on the Advanced plan and
  above.

## Adding partners to a group

There are many ways to add partners to a group, depending on whether they're already enrolled or haven't joined your program yet.

### Inviting partners to apply

After your group is created, when you share the unique application URL, all new applicants who applied through that page will be assigned to that group. The assigned group shows in the **Group** column of the applications table.

### Approving applications

When reviewing a new application, the assigned group is shown in the application's **Group** block. To pick a different group before approving, click **Change** next to it.

### Adding multiple partners to a group

When viewing all your partners, you can use the multi-select function to add one or many partners at a time to any group.

Simply click the checkbox beside their name and click **Change group** to move them to your desired partner group.

## Moving partners between groups

There are a few ways to move partners between groups:

**Via the partner profile page**

On the partner profile page, click **Change** in the **Group** block, select the **New group**, and confirm with **Change group**.

**Via the partner table**

As mentioned above, you can also use the multi-select function in the partners table: select the checkboxes and click **Change group**.

**Via group move rules**

You can also automatically move partners to a new group based on their performance metrics — see group move rules.

### Partner notification emails

When partners are moved to another group, they receive an email informing them of any reward and bounty changes associated with the move.

### Group move logs

For transparency and auditability, we also keep a history of all group moves for each partner – both from manual moves and via group move rules. Open it with the **History** link in the **Group** block of the partner profile page.

This gives you a complete history of a given partner's group membership changes, which can affect their rewards, discounts, and referral links.

## How many partner groups can I create?

All RevRoute Partners customers can create partner groups, with the number allowed based on your plan.

| Plan                                        | Partner groups                           |
| ------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| Business | Up to 3 groups (including Default group) |
| Advanced | Unlimited groups                         |
| Enterprise     | Unlimited groups                         |

pages.title: Configuring referral links for your partner groups
pages.description: Learn how set default referral links, additional links, and UTM parameters for each partner group in your RevRoute partner program

headings.text: Where to find your referral link settings
How partner group changes affect referral links

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

## Where to find your referral link settings

Each partner group has its own referral link settings. To find them, open a group and click **Links** in the top navigation.

## Default referral links

A default link is created during program setup, so new partner groups always have a referral link. You can also set up additional default links that are automatically created when a partner is enrolled in the partner group.

Click **Create link** in the **Default links** block to add more default links.

**Справка.**

  When creating a default link, you'll be asked to enter a **Destination URL**.
  This is the page users land on after clicking a referral link. It’s often your
  homepage or a dedicated program landing page.

**Default Link Behavior**

- **When you create a default link**, a new link is generated for every partner in that group. This includes both current and future partners in that group.
- **When you update a default link's** destination URL, it updates all the corresponding partner links in that group with the destination URL you set.
- **When you delete a default link**, the link remains for existing partners in that group to ensure historical stats/commissions are preserved.

## Additional partner links

You can also let your partners create their own links beyond the defaults:

For your additional partner links, you can specify the following:

- **Link limit**: the maximum number of links partners can create
- **Link formats**: the domains or URLs your partners can create links to (either any page on a domain, or one specific URL)

**Внимание.**

  Ensure the domain you're adding has conversion tracking set up, or your links
  won't be tracking correctly. Learn more here.

## Link settings

Define the link structure and UTM parameters for all partners in the group.

### Link structure

RevRoute supports two referral link formats. Choose based on how you want links to look and where they’ll be shared. Both formats work the same for attribution.

**Справка.**

  You can use any of the referral link types interchangeably – the option above
  is to determine which format is shown in the partner dashboard.

**Option 1: Short Links**

**Format:** `go.yourdomain.com/{partner-link-key}` — on your program’s link domain. Until the domain is set, the example and preview show a `go.example.com` placeholder.

A clean, branded short link that’s easy to remember and perfect for sharing in social posts, bios, or messages.

**Совет.**

  We recommend using short links for several reasons:

  1. Some web browsers block client-side click tracking, which breaks attribution – with `go.yourdomain.com/john` the click will be tracked server-side too, which improves attribution accuracy
  2. Some web browsers drop query params, which breaks attribution as well
  3. It's cleaner ✨

**Option 2: Query Parameter**

**Format:** `yoursite.com?via={partner-link-key}`

Appends the partner name as a query string on your destination URL. Ideal for users who are migrating from Rewardful and want to maintain backwards compatibility for existing partner links.

### UTM parameters

Set default UTM parameters for all links in this group. This gives you group-specific insights in analytics.

When you update a group’s UTM template, all partner links in the
group are refreshed and overwritten with the new UTM tags.

## How partner group changes affect referral links

As mentioned earlier, a partner's link settings are tied to the partner group they're in. When you update a partner's group, or delete groups, their partner links will be updated as well.

### Moving partners to a group

When a partner is moved to a new group, their links automatically update to match the new group’s defaults and UTM parameters.

**Справка.**

  **Why would you move partners?**

  - To promote them from a starter group to a group with a higher reward tier
  - To try out new rewards in a test group
  - To tidy up your structure and general reorganization

### Deleting groups

If you delete a group, all partners in that group are moved to the default group. Their links are updated to match the default group’s settings.

**Справка.**

  **Why would you delete a group?**

  - The campaign has ended
  - You created a duplicate group by mistake
  - A beta trial group is no longer needed

pages.title: Configuring brand and support resources for your partners
pages.description: Provide partners with support, help docs, program terms of service, and brand assets in their dashboard.
pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

Set your partners up for success by providing support, clear documentation, program terms, and brand assets in their dashboard, so they can get started faster, avoid mistakes, and represent your brand consistently.

## Where to find program resources

In your program menu, open **Resources** under **Engagement**. The page has two sections: **Help and support** and **Brand assets**.

## Help and support

To give your partners the best experience, fill in every field in this section and click **Save**.

### Support email

The address partners use to contact you with questions about your program. **This field is required.**

Partner replies to your program emails go to this address. In the partner dashboard, it's available in the **Program support** block via the **Email support** button.

### Messages

**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Advanced plans and
  above.

The **Enable partner messaging** switch turns on the messaging center: you can message partners directly in RevRoute, and they can message you. When messaging is off, partners see a button to email your support address instead.

### Help center

A link to documentation or other self-serve resources that help your partners succeed. In the partner dashboard, it appears in the **Program support** block as **Help center**. The address in the field is just an example — enter your own.

### Terms of service

A link to your partner program's terms of service (usually separate from your product's general terms). In the partner dashboard, it appears in the **Program support** block.

This address is also used in the required **Agree to program terms** checkbox of your program application form. Until it's set, the form editor shows an **Add link** button next to the checkbox that leads to the **Resources** page.

## Brand assets

Add logos, useful links, brand colors, and other files — partners can download and use them from their dashboard.

Each asset you add has a menu for downloading or opening, copying, editing, and deleting it.

### Brand logos

Upload your official logos so partners always have the latest versions. Click **Add logo**, select or drop a file (SVG, JPG, PNG, or WEBP, up to 5 MB), and enter the **File name**.

### Links

Add links to materials that live on your website — for example, brand guidelines or a banners page. Click **Add link**, then enter the **URL** and the **Display name** partners will see.

### Colors

Share your brand colors. Click **Add color**, pick a color from the palette or enter its **Hex** code, and enter the **Color name**.

### Additional files

Add any other materials for your partners — a document or a ZIP archive of up to 10 MB. For example:

- Brand guidelines
- Product presentation
- Banner pack

Click **Add file**, select or drop a file, and enter the **File name**.

pages.title: Setting up your program
pages.description: Step-by-step guide to go from zero to a live partner program on RevRoute.
pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

In this guide, we will walk you through step-by-step how to set up your partner program on RevRoute Partners and start growing your affiliate revenue.

## The flow at a glance

**Getting started**

  Set up your program name, logo, and referral link settings.

**Configure rewards**

  Choose your primary reward type, structure, duration, and amount.

**Invite partners**
Invite your first partners to your program.

**Help and support**

  Add support resources (support email, terms of service, help center) that
  partners see on their dashboard.

**Overview**
Review your selection and create your program.

**Примечание.**

  Migrating from another platform? Check out our migration
  guides or contact
  support.

## Step 1: Getting started

**Goal**: Set up your program name, logo, and referral link settings.

1. **Company name**: The name of your company (e.g., "Acme").
2. **Logo**: Upload a square logo. It appears on your program landing page and in partner materials.
3. **Referral link**: Set the domain and destination for partner links:
   - **Program domain**: connect a domain you own (DNS setup required). Use a domain dedicated to your program (e.g., `refer.yourcompany.com`).
   - **Website URL**: Where visitors go when they click a partner's referral link (e.g., `https://yourcompany.com`).

Click **Continue** to go to the next step.

## Step 2: Configure rewards

**Goal**: Choose your primary reward type, structure, duration, and amount.

1. **Reward type**
   - **Sale**: When customers subscribe to your product (most common for SaaS).
   - **Lead**: For sign-ups and demos.

2. **Commission structure (only for sale rewards)**
   - **Recurring**: Ongoing revenue share (e.g., 15% of each payment for 12 months)
   - **One-off**: Fixed payout per conversion (e.g., 2,000 ₽ per sale)

3. **Duration (only for recurring rewards)**: How long partners earn (e.g., 12 months)

4. **Reward amount**:
   - **Percentage**: Share of revenue (e.g., 15% per sale)
   - **Flat**: Fixed amount per conversion (e.g., 2,000 ₽ per lead)

Select your reward conditions and click **Continue**.

**Совет.**

  You can add more reward conditions and
  partner groups later in your program settings.

## Step 3: Invite partners

**Goal**: Invite your first partners to your program.

**Примечание.**

  You can skip this step and invite partners
  later from the Partners tab.

1. Enter partner **email addresses**.
2. Click **+ Add partner** to add each one.
3. Click **Continue** to proceed (you can also skip and invite later from the Partners tab).

## Step 4: Help and Support

**Goal**: Add support resources (support email, terms of service, help center) that partners see on their dashboard.

1. **Support email (required)**: Email partners can reach you for questions.
2. **Help center URL**: Link to your help docs or FAQ (e.g. `https://yourcompany.com/help`).
3. **Terms of Service URL**: Link to your affiliate/partner terms (e.g. `https://yourcompany.com/legal/affiliates`).

These appear on the partner dashboard. You can add or update them later in your program resources tab.

---

## Step 5: Overview

**Goal**: Review your selection and create your program.

You'll see a summary of:

- **Reward**: e.g. "Earn 15% for the first sale"
- **Referral link type**: e.g. `refer.revroute.ru/{partner-link-key}`
- **Website URL**: Where partner links redirect

Use the pencil icon on each card to edit. When everything looks correct, click **Create program**.

---

## What's next?

**Set up conversion tracking**

    Track conversions and attribute sign-ups and purchases

**Top up the payout balance**

    Connect payouts and top up the balance RevRoute pays partners from

**Create partner groups**

    Segment partners by rewards, discounts, and performance

**Invite your partners**

    Add partners via dashboard, API, or application form

**Configure partner rewards**

    Create flexible reward structures for partners

**Embedded referral dashboard**

    Enroll partners directly from wihin your app

pages.title: Fraud detection
pages.description: Safeguard your partner program by automatically flagging, reviewing, and resolving suspicious activity.
pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Advanced plans and
  above.

## Using fraud detection

The **Fraud protection** section of the program menu (under **Insights**) helps you catch and act on suspicious partner activity: RevRoute flags events, and you review the details and make the call.

While there are no flagged events, the section says "No events pending review".

Once events appear, the table has these columns:

- **Event** — the fraud event type;
- **Partner** — the partner associated with the event;
- **Last detected** — the date and time of the most recent occurrence.

Each row is a single event type for a given partner and can contain multiple occurrences. If a partner is flagged for different events, they get several rows. You can filter the table by reason and partner.

## Fraud event types

| Event                                  | Description                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cross-program ban                      | The partner has been banned from one or more other programs, indicating a potentially high-risk history. Details such as links, evidence, or notes aren't shared between programs. |
| Duplicate payout method                | The partner uses a payout method already linked to another partner account, which may indicate duplicate accounts or fraud.             |
| Matching customer email                | The partner's email matches the customer's email — a possible self-referral.                                                            |
| Suspicious customer email domain       | The customer's email uses a disposable or temporary domain — a possible fraud attempt.                                                  |
| Banned referral source (configurable)  | The conversion, event, or click came from a banned referral domain.                                                                     |
| Paid traffic (configurable)            | The conversion, event, or click came from paid advertising traffic.                                                                     |
| Fraud report                           | Another program reported this partner for suspected fraud — e.g. when rejecting their application.                                     |

## Reviewing fraud events

**Внимание.**

  We recommend reviewing flagged events carefully and reaching out to the
  partner if needed before making a final decision.

Click any row in the table to open the **Event review** sheet. It has three blocks:

1. The partner associated with the event — from here you can **Message** them or open their **Partner profile**.
2. The event details: type, description, and a row for each occurrence of this type for the partner.
3. The partner's pending commissions that occurred after the flagged event.

## Resolving fraud events

Take your time and investigate before deciding. For example:

1. Compare partner and customer profiles to see whether they are duplicates or self-referrals.
2. Check your sales data for fraud signals (e.g. anti-fraud reports from your payment provider).
3. Ask the partner about their referral activity via our built-in messaging center.

Once you're confident in your findings, choose one of the actions below.

### Resolve fraud event

If the event is benign, click **Resolve event** to mark it as safe and keep the partner in your program. When confirming, you can add a note on why the event was resolved and what you checked.

### Ban partner

If the fraud is confirmed, click **Ban partner** to mark the event as fraudulent and ban the partner from your program. Their other events pending review are resolved automatically.

You'll also need to pick a ban reason:

| Reason                              | When to use it                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Terms of Service violation          | The partner violated your program rules or the RevRoute terms of use.                                 |
| Inappropriate or offensive content  | The partner associated your brand or program link with harmful, explicit, or inappropriate content.   |
| Artificial traffic                  | The partner inflated traffic with bots, fake clicks, or other methods.                                |
| Fraudulent activity                 | The partner generated fake clicks, leads, or other tracked actions to earn rewards.                   |
| Spam or misleading content          | The partner used deceptive messaging, false claims, impersonation, or aggressive promotion.           |
| Brand or trademark violation        | The partner misused your brand name or trademarks or caused confusion.                                |

## Resolved fraud events

To view resolved events, open the **⋮** menu in the top right corner of the page and select **View resolved**. The **Resolved events** list shows when each event was resolved and the note left. Click any row to open the details.

## Fraud settings

Some detection rules can be configured: click **Fraud settings** in the top right corner of the page.

### Paid traffic

This rule flags traffic from paid ads. If your program doesn't allow partners to run ads, turn it on and pick the ad networks to flag: Google, Facebook, X, Bing, LinkedIn, Reddit, and TikTok each have their own toggle.

#### Google campaign IDs whitelist

Add your internal Google Campaign IDs here to prevent your own Google Ads traffic from being flagged as fraudulent and associated with a partner.

**Совет.**

  **Why this matters for Dynamic Search Ads (DSA):** If you run DSA campaigns, Google crawls your site and automatically selects landing pages to serve as ads. Sometimes Google indexes pages that already contain affiliate tracking parameters (e.g., `?via=affiliate`) from affiliate links being shared around the web.

When these pages are served as ads, the affiliate parameter carries through – making it appear that an affiliate is running unauthorized paid ads when it's actually your own campaign. Whitelisting your Google Campaign IDs ensures this internal traffic is correctly attributed to you and not flagged as partner fraud.

### Referral source

This rule flags traffic from specific domains. Turn it on and add the domains you want to monitor. Use the `*` wildcard to match any part of the address — handy for monitoring a specific page rather than all traffic from a domain.

### Disabling fraud settings

When you disable an active rule, RevRoute offers to mark the pending events for that rule as resolved.

pages.title: Measuring program performance
pages.description: Track conversion rates, referral sources, UTM parameters, geolocation data and more to understand ROI and performance of your partner program.

headings.text: Where to find your program analytics?
3. Aggregated data for different facets (top views)

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

On any given day, RevRoute tracks upwards of **5 million clicks, conversion, and commission events.**

With the sheer volume of data that's tracked, it is important to be able to easily filter and create reports to help marketing teams make informed decisions.

In this guide, we'll walk you through how to use the program analytics tab get the most out of your partner program's events and engagement data.

## Where to find your program analytics?

When viewing your Partner Program navigation, click on the **Analytics** page, in the **Insights** group:

## Program analytics views

Your program analytics dashboard consists of several views:

1. Analytics chart
2. Partner data table
3. Aggregated data for different facets (top views)

### 1. Analytics chart

This is the default view and shows you the number of click events in a time-series chart over time. You can also select leads or sales to view their chart and data.

**Data toggle**

You can change the data displayed by clicking the `123 | $` toggle in the top right of the data type section.

By default `$` is selected, as it related directly to your reward types. Switching to `123` will change any monetary values to their specific reward count. If your program has other monetary rewards (clicks, leads, sales), their dollar amount will show as well.

**Chart toggle**

You can change the chart type displayed by clicking the `time-chart | conversion funnel` toggle in the top right of the chart area.

When the chart type is switched to **conversion funnel**, you can view the percentage of customers that complete each stage of the sale conversion. In this example, 0.58% of clicks have resulted in a customer making a purchase.

### 2. Partner data table

This table shows your partners performance for each of the data types from the time-series chart (clicks, leads, and sales). The matching data column is sorted by most-to-least, so you can quickly see who is the top performer for that category.

### 3. Aggregated data for different facets (top views)

These are more commonly known as the "Top Views" in RevRoute Analytics. These views show your top links, countries, cities, devices, and more.

Each section has their own tabs to select different data for you to explore your program data further. These are grouped by the following categories:

- **Links** - Short Links and Destination URLs
- **Referrals** - Referrers and UTM Parameters
- **Location** - Countries, Cities, Regions, and Continents
- **Tech** - Devices, Browser, OS, and Triggers

## Filtering your data

With all this data, it's important to be able to filter and make better decisions. You can click the **Filter** button in the top left will show you the options available.

| Filter    | Description                                                                                          |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Ask AI    | Use natural language to query your analytics - eg: "mobile chrome users US only", "UK android users" |
| Group     | Select a specific partner group                                                                      |
| Partner   | Select a specific program partner                                                                    |
| Country   | Select a specific county                                                                             |
| City      | Select a specific city                                                                               |
| Continent | Select a specific continent - N. America, Europe, etc                                                |
| Device    | Select a specific device - Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, etc                                              |
| Browser   | Select a specific browser - Chrome, Safari, Firefox, etc                                             |
| OS        | Select a specific operating system - Windows, Mac OS, etc                                            |
| Referer   | Select the specific website a visitor arrived from                                                   |

pages.title: Migrating from FirstPromoter
pages.description: Easily migrate your affiliate program from FirstPromoter to RevRoute Partners in just a few clicks.

headings.text: How to migrate from FirstPromoter to RevRoute?
1. Connect payouts and top up the balance
2. Notify your affiliates about the platform change

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  RevRoute Partners is only available on Business plans and
  above.

FirstPromoter is a practical option for companies just starting out with their affiliate programs.

If you're moving your program to RevRoute Partners, here's what you get:

1. **Partner payouts in rubles**: RevRoute pays your partners for you — self-employed partners and sole proprietors through RocketWork, legal entities to their settlement account from a nominal account at T-Bank.
2. **Flexible rewards**: 3 reward types — per click, per lead, and per sale (flat or percentage), reward conditions — e.g. a higher rate for customers from a specific country — and bounties.
3. **Analytics**: conversion tracking and stats by source, device, and country, including natural-language queries.
4. **Embedded referral dashboard** (Advanced plan and above): embed a referral dashboard right in your app.
5. **Offer marketplace** (Enterprise plan): your program is listed in the RevRoute catalogue, where partners find and join offers themselves.

In this article, we'll learn how to import your FirstPromoter affiliate program to RevRoute Partners for a more powerful and scalable partner management experience.

## How to migrate from FirstPromoter to RevRoute?

If you're looking to migrate from FirstPromoter to RevRoute Partners, we've built a custom migration tool that will help you migrate everything over in just 2-3 clicks – without breaking any existing FirstPromoter affiliate links.

**Add a custom domain to your RevRoute workspace**

Before starting the migration process, you'll need to add a custom domain to RevRoute. This domain will be used to create short links for each affiliate link that we import from FirstPromoter.

If you haven't added a custom domain to RevRoute yet, you can follow this guide to set that up.

**Set up conversion tracking + client-side click-tracking**

Next, set up conversion tracking to track signup and sale events. We also have some in-app guides that you can reference here.

For backward compatibility, we also recommend setting up client-side click-tracking when installing the RevRoute Analytics script on your site. This will ensure all your existing `domain.com?fp_ref=affiliate` links will keep working as expected, which gives affiliates time to update their links to the new format.

The client-side installation guide walks through enabling click tracking for your RevRoute short links.

**Get your FirstPromoter API Key and Account ID**

Follow this guide to get your FirstPromoter API key – API keys can be created in the Settings tab of your FirstPromoter dashboard.

You will also need to get your FirstPromoter Account ID under your Settings tab as well.

We will use the API key and Account ID to retrieve and import your existing FirstPromoter affiliate program campaigns to RevRoute.

**Import your FirstPromoter campaign**

Once you've set up your RevRoute partner program, open the import dialog with this direct link: app.revroute.ru/program/partners?import=firstpromoter. For now, the **Partners** section menu doesn't have an import option.

Enter your **FirstPromoter API Key** and **FirstPromoter Account ID**, then click **Start Import**.

## What data is migrated?

Our FirstPromoter migration tool imports the following attributes to RevRoute Partners:

### Campaigns / Groups

Each of your campaigns on FirstPromoter will be mapped to a partner group on RevRoute.

**Справка.**

  Since FirstPromoter doesn't expose a `/rewards` endpoint, your FirstPromoter
  program terms will not be migrated – all partners will be assigned to your
  program's default reward.

Learn more about how Partner
rewards work on RevRoute.

### Promoters / Partners

To ensure the efficiency of your partner program, we automatically filter out dormant promoters and only import the ones that both:

- Are in an "accepted" state (docs)
- Have at least 1 referral (docs)

We also automatically import all your promoters' links and recreate them in RevRoute using your program's domain and default URL.

### Referrals / Customers

By default, we import all referrals that are associated with an affiliate in your FirstPromoter program. This ensures that all subsequent subscription renewal events will continue to be tracked on RevRoute.

**Внимание.**

  Some referrals might not have a valid billing-system customer ID yet. They
  will still be imported, with the customer ID filled in once the next billing
  event arrives.

### Commissions

We also import all commissions associated with any customers that were imported above. Depending on the commission state on FirstPromoter, they will be marked accordingly on RevRoute as well:
| FirstPromoter | RevRoute |
| --- | --- |
| `Pending` | `Pending` |
| `Approved` | `Processed` |
| `Denied` | `Canceled` |

RevRoute also supports 4 additional commission states:

- `Paid`: When the payout containing the commission has been paid.
- `Refunded`: If the sale for the commission was refunded.
- `Fraud`: Useful for marking a sale as fraudulent and excluding it from any future payouts.
- `Duplicate`: Useful for marking if a commission was rewarded more than once and needs to be marked as a duplicate event.

**Внимание.**

  Commissions for referrals that do not have a valid billing-system customer ID or a
  transaction trace will not be imported.

If there are any other attributes that you'd like to see migrated (or if you would like to customize any of the rules above), please send us an email to let us know!

## Next steps

After importing your program, here are some recommended next steps:

### 1. Connect payouts and top up the balance

RevRoute Partners supports 1-click payouts: earnings are aggregated and paid out in rubles — to self-employed partners and sole proprietors through RocketWork, to legal entities from a nominal account at T-Bank.

Before your first payout:

1. Fill in **Company details** under **Settings → Billing** — RevRoute then connects the payout channels.
2. Top up your payout balance: the RocketWork account and/or the nominal account.

If you pay partners yourself outside RevRoute, choose the Manual payout method — then you don't need a balance.

### 2. Notify your affiliates about the platform change

Next, you'll want to reach out to your existing partners and let them know about the platform change. To do that, you can send them an email with the following example verbiage:

> Hey,
>
> Starting today, we are switching the [Your Company] Affiliate Program from FirstPromoter to RevRoute Partners.
>
> To get started, follow these steps:
>
> 1. Sign up for a RevRoute Partners account here: `partners.revroute.ru/{your_program_slug}/register`
> 2. Set your tax status (self-employed, sole proprietor or legal entity) in payout settings to receive your commissions.
> 3. Start sharing your shiny new referral link with your audience 🚀
>
> Let us know if you have any questions!

If you pay partners manually, drop step 2: partners don't need a tax status in that case.

## Need help?

If you need help migrating your program, contact us.
