pages.title: RevRoute Partners Overview
pages.description: Kickstart viral product-led growth with powerful, branded referral and affiliate programs with RevRoute Partners.

headings.text: Referral + affiliate program built in one

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

In today's day and age, especially with the rise of AI, the best ideas and products are no longer sufficient to rise above the competition and become a category leader.

What works is having a powerful distribution network that can produce consistent, repeatable, and profitable results – ideally on autopilot. A good example of this is a product-led partner program, be it a referral or an affiliate program.

Think Dropbox's famous "Refer a friend" program, or Framer's beloved Partner Program that generates $8M worth of payouts annually.

**This is where RevRoute Partners comes in.**

With RevRoute Partners, you can build powerful, scalable referral _and_ affiliate programs with **1-click payouts** and **white-labeling functionality**.

## How does RevRoute Partners work?

RevRoute Partners is an all-in-one partner management platform for you to scale your revenue by incentivizing both your users and external partners to help spread the word about your product.

1. **You create a program** – Set up your partner program, define reward rules (e.g., % of sale, fixed amount per lead), and configure payouts.
2. **Partners join and get links** – Partners apply or are invited, then receive unique tracking links (short links or query-parameter links).
3. **Visitors click and convert** – When someone clicks a partner link and later signs up or buys, RevRoute attributes that conversion to the partner.
4. **Commissions are calculated** – RevRoute applies your reward rules and creates commissions.
5. **Partners get paid** – You can pay via RevRoute (self-employed partners and sole proprietors through RocketWork, legal entities from a nominal account at T-Bank) or pay them yourself outside the platform.

RevRoute Partners is built on the same attribution infrastructure as RevRoute short links.

## Key concepts

| Concept           | What it means                                                                                                    |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Program**       | Your partner program (e.g., "Acme Affiliate Program"). Each workspace can have one program.                      |
| **Partner**       | A person or company in your program who shares links and earns commissions.                                      |
| **Partner group** | A tier or segment of partners (e.g., "Affiliates", "VIP Partners") with its own reward rules and link structure. |
| **Reward rules**  | How partners earn: per click, per lead, per sale, or a mix. You define these per group.                          |
| **Conversion**    | A tracked action (lead or sale) that gets attributed to a partner link.                                          |
| **Commission**    | The amount a partner earns from a conversion, based on your reward rules.                                        |

## RevRoute Partners features

With RevRoute Partners, you can:

1. Launch referral & affiliate programs with your users and external partners
2. Create flexible reward structures (pay-per-click, lead, sale) tailored to each partner
3. Send payouts to partners in 1 click – in rubles, to self-employed partners, sole proprietors and legal entities
4. Offer dual-sided incentives to users who sign up through your partners
5. Generate a program landing page with AI to drive partner signups
6. Create an embedded referral dashboard inside your app

### Referral + affiliate program built in one

With RevRoute Partners, you can launch both referral and affiliate programs with your users and external partners – all in a single platform.

This allows you to maximize your revenue growth by partnering with your most avid users and the best content creators in your niche, without needing to manage them in separate systems.

### Flexible reward structures

With RevRoute, you can create advanced pay-per-click/lead and rev-share reward structures to drive partner engagement and revenue.

| Reward type                     | Description                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Click-based (pay-per-click)** | Rewarding partners for driving clicks to your product – similar to how Google Ads' pay-per-click works.                                            |
| **Lead-based (pay-per-lead)**   | A more effective alternative to pay-per-click, where you reward partners for leads generated (e.g. demo requests, free trial signups, etc.)        |
| **Sale-based (pay-per-sale)**   | This is the most common reward type, where you reward partners for driving sales to your product either via a rev-share or fixed-price commission. |

Learn more about how to create partner rewards on RevRoute Partners.

### 1-click partner payouts

RevRoute Partners supports 1-click payouts: you top up the payout balance and confirm the invoice, and RevRoute transfers commissions to each partner.

If you're running a partner program with hundreds of partners, there's no need to send each payout manually: RevRoute pays self-employed partners and sole proprietors through RocketWork, with a one-off contract for every payout, and legal entities from a nominal account at T-Bank to their settlement account. Individuals without a tax status can't be paid.

Partners pay their own taxes: for self-employed partners RocketWork issues the NPD receipt, sole proprietors and legal entities report under their own tax regime. Learn more about taxes.

### Dual-sided incentives

With RevRoute Partners, you can create dual-sided incentives for your affiliate/referral programs, which give special discounts to customers who sign up via a referral link.

Some examples include:

- 25% discount for the first 12 months
- 30% lifetime discount
- ₽5,000 one-off discount

This can drive powerful word-of-mouth growth as partners are more likely to share their link if it gives their audience additional discounts, and their users are more likely to click on their links if they're getting a special deal.

Learn more about how to create dual-sided incentives for your partner program.

### AI landing page generator

You can also use our intelligent AI landing page generator to create a compelling, branded landing page for your program to drive partner signups.

Learn more about how to create a branded landing page with RevRoute Partners.

### Embedded referral dashboard

One of the unique features of RevRoute Partners is the ability to create an embedded referral dashboard directly inside your application.

This allows you to seamlessly onboard your users to your referral program, without them needing to leave your app and sign up on a third-party platform.

Learn how to set it up in the embedded referral dashboard guide.

## Get started

With RevRoute Partners, you can build a powerful, scalable word-of-mouth flywheel by incentivizing both your users and external partners to help you grow.

To get started with RevRoute Partners, follow our program quickstart and conversion tracking guides.

## Related articles

**Setting up your program**

    Step-by-step guide from zero to a live partner program

**Conversion tracking**

    Track conversions and attribute sign-ups and purchases

**Partner groups**

    Segment partners by rewards, discounts, and performance

**Inviting partners**

    Add partners via dashboard, API, or application form

**Partner rewards**

    Create flexible reward structures for partners

**Embedded referral dashboard**

    Enroll partners directly from wihin your app

pages.title: Inviting partners to your program
pages.description: Learn how to invite partners to join your affiliate/referral program on RevRoute Partners
pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

There are a few ways you can invite partners to join your affiliate/referral program on RevRoute Partners:

1. Inviting via the dashboard
2. Enrolling a partner automatically
3. Via a branded application form

## Inviting via the dashboard

The easiest way to invite a partner to join your program is by sending them an invitation email.

Open **All partners** in the program menu and click **Invite partner** (or press `P`).

The **Invite partner** sheet opens. Enter the partner's email and, optionally, their name, short link (the address of their referral link), and the group they're being added to. Below is a preview of the email the partner will receive; it's sent from `notifications@revroute.ru`.

### Bulk Invitations

Invite multiple partners at once by separating their email addresses with commas or pasting a list into the **Email** field. Each partner receives an individual invitation email.

### Updating invitation email

You're also able to edit the email that is sent to the invited partner. To do this, click **Edit** in the **Email preview** section.

You can change the email **Subject**, **Title**, and **Content**. Style the content with the buttons under the editor: bold, italic, and link. Changes apply only to this invite — they don't replace the default content.

Click **Save** to update the email content, or **Cancel** to revert back to the default content. Once your invite is ready to send, click **Send invite**. Your partner will receive an email in their inbox to join your program.

### Viewing past invites

To view your previous invites, on the **All partners** page click **Filter**, then **Status**, then **Invited**.

The **⋯** menu on an invited partner's row lets you resend the invite, delete the invite, or change the group. Deleting an invite can't be undone.

## Enrolling a partner automatically

Instead of sending an invitation email and waiting for them to accept it, you can also automatically enroll known partners in your program.

A few use cases for this approach:

- Programmatically adding your apps users to your in-app referral program
- Migrating your partners over from another platform like Rewardful

If you're integrating with RevRoute Partners programatically, you can use our POST /partners API endpoint to enroll a partner into your program via our API.

**Внимание.**

  Before auto-enrolling a partner to your program, make sure to get their
  consent – either explicitly or via the acceptance of your Terms of Service.
  Enrolling partners that are unfamiliar with your program is against our terms
  of service.

## Via a branded application form

Alternatively, you can also have your partners apply via a branded application form:

Learn more about how to create a branded application form with RevRoute Partners.

pages.title: Customizing your program application form
pages.description: Learn how to customize your program application form to collect the right information you need and select the best partners to work with for your program.

headings.text: What is the program application form?
Where to find the application form builder?

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

## What is the program application form?

The program application form collects the information you want from people applying to your program. Use it to ask about websites, social accounts, experience, audience size, or any details that help you decide who to accept.

The form lives at `partners.revroute.ru/<program-slug>/apply` — the **Apply** button on your program landing page leads there. Submitted applications appear under **Applications**.

**Совет.**

  On RevRoute, you can create a separate application form for each partner
  group — e.g. ask
  bloggers about their audience and integrators about their clients.

A new partner group starts with a copy of the default group's application form,
which you can then edit separately.

## Where to find the application form builder?

On the **Groups** page, open the partner group you want to tailor the application form for:

Open the **Branding** tab and choose **Application form** in the switcher above the editor. For your program's default group, here's a quick link straight to the form builder.

## Mandatory fields

**Name**, **Email**, and **Country** are required in every form and always come first — you cannot remove or rename them. The heading and description above the form can only be edited, which keeps the page layout consistent for applicants.

## Editing and adding fields

Hover over a field to reveal its actions: **Edit** (pencil), **Move up** and **Move down** (arrows), and a trash icon that deletes the field. The **Insert field** button between fields adds a new field at that spot.

## Input field types

Click **Insert field** and pick the input type:

### Short text

Use for short answers like names, links, or one-line bios.

| Option            | Details                               | Example                                 |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Field label       | The question above the field          | _"Link to your website or social page"_ |
| Field placeholder | Guidance shown inside the empty field | `https://t.me/your_channel`             |
| Required          | Make the field mandatory              | Yes                                     |
| Max characters    | Set a character limit                 | 120                                     |

### Long text

Use for longer responses that need multiple lines. The options are the same as for short text.

| Option            | Details                               | Example                           |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Field label       | The question above the field          | _"Tell us about your audience"_   |
| Field placeholder | Guidance shown inside the empty field | _"Topics, reach, platforms"_      |
| Required          | Make the field mandatory              | No                                |
| Max characters    | Set a character limit                 | 500                               |

### Dropdown

Best when you have many options. You can add, delete, and reorder options by dragging.

| Option      | Details                          | Example                                                  |
| ----------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field label | The question above the field     | _"Where do you recommend products?"_                     |
| Required    | Make the field mandatory         | Yes                                                      |
| Options     | The choices the applicant sees   | _"Telegram channel"_, _"VK"_, _"YouTube"_, _"Website or blog"_ |

### Multiple choice

All options are visible at once — handy for a short set of answers. By default, applicants pick one option; turn on **Allow multiple selections** to let them pick several.

| Option                    | Details                          | Example                                                 |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| Field label               | The question above the field     | _"What is your content about?"_                         |
| Required                  | Make the field mandatory         | No                                                      |
| Allow multiple selections | Several answers instead of one   | Yes                                                     |
| Options                   | The choices the applicant sees   | _"Tech & SaaS"_, _"Business & Finance"_, _"Marketing"_  |

### Image upload

Let applicants attach images — e.g. analytics screenshots or work samples. JPG, PNG, and WebP files up to 5 MB are accepted.

| Option                | Details                                         | Example                           |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Field label           | The question above the field                    | _"Audience analytics screenshots"_ |
| Allow multiple images | Several files instead of one; set a maximum from 2 to 10 | Yes, up to 5              |
| Required              | Make the field mandatory                        | No                                |

### Website and socials

Ask for the applicant's website and social accounts. Toggle each platform on or off — website, Instagram, YouTube, X/Twitter, TikTok, LinkedIn — and mark any required. For example, you might require a website but make YouTube optional.

**Совет.**

  You can only add one website and socials field per form: once it's there, the
  type no longer appears in the **Insert field** dialog. Ask for a Telegram
  channel or VK page with a short text field.

## Program terms agreement

The form ends with a required **Program terms agreement** checkbox. The **Add link** button next to it opens the **Resources** page, where you set your terms URL in the **Terms of use** field.

## Publishing your changes

As with the landing page, unpublished changes are marked **Unsaved draft** and exist only in your browser. When the form is ready, click **Publish** in the top right corner of the editor.

pages.title: Reviewing program applications
pages.description: Learn how to manage your pending applications, and to bring the best partners to your program.

headings.text: Where to find your program applications

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

## Where to find your program applications

In the program menu, open **Applications** under **Partners**. The count badge next to it shows how many applications are waiting for review.

## Applicant table

On your applications table, you'll be able to view key information, including:

- The applicant's name
- When they applied
- The group they applied to
- Their country
- Their website and social media profiles — e.g. YouTube and LinkedIn

**Filter** narrows applications down by group and country, and the search box finds an applicant by name, email, or company. Click on any of the rows to open the application.

## Applications menu

The **⋮** menu in the top right corner of the page has:

- **Auto-approval settings** — opens the default group's settings (see Auto-approve);
- **View rejected partners** — the list of rejected applications (see below);
- **Export as CSV** — downloads the applications.

## Partner application

The application sheet brings together everything the applicant shared:

- the **About partner** tab — answers to your application form questions, description, website, and social profiles;
- on the right — name, email, country, and application date;
- **Risk analysis** — see risk flags;
- **Program activity** — how many RevRoute programs the partner is active in and how many they are banned from;
- **Group** — the group they applied to; change it with **Change**.

On the **Comments** tab, your team can leave notes about the applicant — they're visible only in your workspace. The **Message** button opens a conversation with the applicant in **Messages**, and the arrows at the top switch between applications.

### Online presence

Partners add their website and social accounts to their profile and can verify that they own them. Verification is optional but speeds up review: if no platforms are added or verified, a matching risk flag appears in the risk analysis.

## Applicant risk flags

**Совет.**

  Application risk analysis is available on Advanced plans and
  above.

**Внимание.**

  We recommend reviewing flagged applicants and the information they've
  provided before making a final decision.

The **Risk analysis** block in the application sheet shows the overall risk level — **Low**, **Medium**, or **High** — and the flags behind it. The **Open** button shows all flags with explanations.

These signals are powered by fraud detection:

| Flag                                | Level  | Description                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------- | ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Fraud report                        | High   | This partner has been flagged for suspected fraud by another program.                                                    |
| Cross-program ban                   | High   | This partner has been banned from one or more other RevRoute programs, indicating a potentially high-risk history.       |
| Duplicate payout method             | High   | This partner is using a payout method already linked to another partner account, which may indicate duplicate accounts or fraud. |
| No website or social links added    | Medium | This partner hasn't provided any website or social links, making verification difficult.                                |
| Email domain mismatch with website  | Low    | The custom email domain doesn't match the provided website.                                                              |
| Masked email address                | Low    | Uses an anonymized email address. Not harmful, but harder to verify and to contact directly.                              |
| No verified website or social links | Low    | This partner hasn't verified their website or socials, making verification difficult.                                   |

## Approving applicants

There are 3 ways to approve pending applicants into your program.

### From the application sheet

Click **Approve** at the bottom of the application sheet (or press `A`) — the applicant joins your program right away.

### Bulk approve

Select applicants with the checkboxes on the left (the header checkbox selects everyone) and click **Approve** above the table.

### Auto-approve

Auto-approve is set per partner group: open the group, go to the **Settings** tab, and turn on **Enable auto-approve** under **Additional settings**. For the default group, **Auto-approval settings** in the applications menu leads there too.

RevRoute asks you to confirm. Check **Apply to all groups** to enable auto-approve in every group of the program at once.

From then on, new applications to the group are approved automatically without review. Existing pending applications still need manual approval. Turning auto-approve off works the same way — with the toggle and a confirmation.

## Rejecting applicants

You can reject an application from the application sheet — with **Reject** or the `R` key — or several at once by selecting them in the table.

A **Reject application** confirmation dialog opens first. If you suspect fraud, check **Select this if you believe the application shows signs of fraud**: the report helps protect other RevRoute programs — the partner gets a "Fraud report" flag. **Reject** rejects the application, **Cancel** backs out.

A rejected applicant can't join your program unless you approve their application yourself.

### Approving a previously rejected partner

If you rejected a partner by mistake or changed your mind, open the **⋮** menu on the applications page and select **View rejected partners**. In the **Rejected applications** list, open the application and click **Approve** — the partner joins your program right away.

pages.title: Creating a landing page for your partner program
pages.description: Create an effective and compelling landing page to attract high-quality partners to join your program and promote your product.

headings.text: What is the program landing page?
Where to find the landing page builder?
Generating your landing page with AI

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

On RevRoute, you can create a branded landing page with details about your partner program.

## What is the program landing page?

The program landing page tells potential partners about your program and the rewards offered. You can add a product description, brand materials, FAQ sections, and any other content that helps an applicant understand why they should apply.

The landing page is published at `partners.revroute.ru/<program-slug>` — for example, partners.revroute.ru/cloudflow-demo for the CloudFlow demo program. Its **Apply** button leads to your application form.

**Совет.**

  On RevRoute, you can create a separate landing page for each partner
  group — e.g. different
  pages for bloggers, integrators, and resellers. A group's landing page lives at
  `partners.revroute.ru/<program-slug>/<group-slug>`.

A new partner group starts with a copy of the default group's landing page,
which you can then edit separately.

## Where to find the landing page builder?

On the **Groups** page, open the group you want to customize the landing page for:

Open the **Branding** tab and choose **Landing page** in the switcher above the editor. The **Branding** item in the program menu (under **Configuration**) also leads to the default group's landing page.

On the left are the **Brand elements**: logo (required), wordmark, and brand color, saved with their own **Save** button. On the right is the landing page preview, which you edit in place. The **Open** button above the preview opens the landing page in a new tab.

## Editing and adding content

Hover over a landing page block to reveal its actions: **Edit** (pencil), **Move up** and **Move down** (arrows), and a trash icon that deletes the block. The **Insert block** button between blocks adds a new block at that spot.

The top section is the same on every landing page: eyebrow, heading, description, the **Rewards** block, and the **Apply** button. The heading and description can only be edited — this keeps every group's page consistent. Rewards come from the group settings. Blocks below the **Apply** button can be added, edited, removed, and reordered.

## Content types

Clicking **Insert block** lets you pick the content type:

### Text

Best for describing your product and program terms. Set a **Section title** and **Content** — the content supports Markdown (see the table below).

### Image

For product screenshots and other visuals. Upload an SVG, JPG, PNG, or WebP file up to 5 MB and fill in the **Alt text**.

### Files

A list of downloadable files — e.g. logos or a product deck. For each file, set a **Display name**, **File URL**, and an optional **Description**; **Add item** adds another file. Files aren't uploaded to RevRoute — the block links to them by URL.

### Accordion

Collapsible items — best for FAQ sections. Each item has a **Title** and **Content**; **Add item** adds another one, and you can reorder items by dragging the handle on the left.

### Earnings calculator

Gives partners a sense of how much they can earn. Set the **Average product price** (in rubles) and the **Billing period**: monthly, yearly, or one-time. Earnings are calculated from your program's default reward, and visitors pick the number of sales with a slider.

## Generating your landing page with AI

The AI landing page generator can quickly scaffold a page from your website: it reads the site's content and drafts blocks about your company, pricing, features, and more.

Click **Generate** above the preview and check the **Website URL** — it's prefilled from your program settings. Then click **Generate** in the dialog.

**Внимание.**

  AI can make mistakes – make sure to review all generated content for accuracy
  and style before publishing your changes.

## Publishing your changes

Until you publish, the editor shows an **Unsaved draft** label and partners keep seeing the previous version of the page. The draft is stored only in your browser, so teammates see your changes once they're published.

When you're done, click **Publish** in the top right corner of the editor. The **⋮** menu next to it has an **Unpublish** option.

## Markdown styles available

| Content         | Example                                 |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Headings        | `# H1`, `## H2`, `### H3`               |
| Bold            | `**bold text**`                         |
| Italic          | `*italicized text*`                     |
| Blockquote      | `> blockquote`                          |
| Horizontal rule | `---`                                   |
| Link            | `title`      |
| Ordered list    | `1. First item`, `2. Second item`       |
| Unordered list  | `- First item`, `- Second item`         |

pages.title: Managing partner commissions
pages.description: Learn how partner commissions work on RevRoute, and how to create manual commissions or clawbacks (negative commissions).

headings.text: Where to find your program commissions?

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

## Where to find your program commissions?

In the program menu, open **Commissions** under **Insights**. The top of the page summarizes how many commissions you have and for what amount — in total, pending, processed, and paid. Below is the table of all program commissions with a filter and a date range picker.

| Column      | Data                                                                         |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Date        | Commission date                                                              |
| Customer    | The customer associated with the lead or sale                                |
| Partner     | The partner receiving the commission                                         |
| Type        | Click, lead, sale, referral, or "Other" — the label for manual one-time commissions |
| Sale amount | The sale amount, or a count for clicks, leads, and manual commissions        |
| Commission  | The amount the partner will receive                                          |
| Status      | The current commission status — see below            |

Use the gear button in the table header to choose columns — for example, add **Group**. To download commissions, use the **⋮** menu → **Export as CSV**.

## Commission statuses

A new commission moves through these statuses:

- **Pending** — the initial status. The commission waits for the partner group's payout holding period — from zero to 90 days.
- **Processed** — the holding period is over and the commission is available for payout.
- **Paid** — the payout containing this commission has been sent.

A commission can also get one of these statuses:

- **Refunded** — the sale behind the commission was refunded. Set automatically when your billing system passes the refund event, or via the RevRoute API.
- **Fraud** — the commission was deemed fraudulent.
- **Duplicate** — the commission was deemed a duplicate and excluded from all upcoming payouts.
- **Canceled** — the commission was canceled, e.g. for a self-referral sale.
- **On hold** — the commission is paused, e.g. while fraud events are being reviewed.

To mark a commission manually, use the **⋯** menu on its row: **Mark as duplicate**, **Mark as fraud**, or **Cancel commission**. RevRoute asks you to confirm — **the action can't be undone**. Marking as fraud and canceling can be applied to all past and future commissions of the same customer–partner pair.

## Creating manual commissions

Sometimes you need to create a commission manually — e.g. to pay a bonus or account for a sale missed due to a tracking error. Manual commissions are included in the partner's next payout.

Click **Create commission** (or press `C`) on the **Commissions** page or in a partner's profile. In the **Create commission** sheet, pick the partner and the commission type: **One-time**, **Lead**, or **Recurring sale**.

### One-time commissions

A bonus, reimbursement, or any other payout not tied to a customer, referral link, or sale.

| Field           | Description                              | Required |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Amount          | The commission amount in rubles          | ✅       |
| Description     | An optional description, up to 190 characters | ❌  |
| Set custom date | The commission date; defaults to today   | ❌       |

### Lead commissions

A reward for a qualified sign-up or referral. The amount is calculated automatically from the lead reward of the partner's group.

| Field                      | Description                                                                          | Required |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- |
| Referral link              | The partner link the lead is tied to                                                 | ✅       |
| Customer                   | The customer associated with the lead; you can create a new one right here | ✅ |
| Set custom lead event date | The event date; defaults to today                                                    | ❌       |
| Set custom lead event name | The lead event name                                                                  | ❌       |

### Recurring sale commissions

A reward for a subscription payment by a referred customer. The commission is calculated from the sale reward once you enter the sale amount.

| Field         | Description                                                                  | Required |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Referral link | The partner link the sale is tied to; available once a partner is selected  | ✅       |
| Customer      | The customer associated with the sale; you can create a new one right here | ✅ |
| Sale amount   | The sale amount in rubles; appears once a customer is selected               | ✅       |
| Set sale date | The sale date; defaults to today                                             | ❌       |
| Invoice ID    | The sale's invoice ID — can be used to retrieve the commission via the API   | ❌       |
| Product ID    | The ID of the product sold                                                   | ❌       |

### Creating a new customer

If the customer doesn't exist in RevRoute yet, open the **Customer** list and select **Create new customer** to open the **New customer** dialog.

| Field       | Description                                                                            | Required |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- |
| Name        | The customer's name                                                                    | ❌       |
| Email       | The customer's email                                                                   | ❌       |
| Country     | The customer's country — used in analytics and country-specific rewards; Russia by default | ✅   |
| External ID | Your unique ID for this customer — e.g. your database ID or email                      | ✅       |

Once created, you can attach commissions to the customer.

## Creating clawbacks

If a partner was credited too much, create a clawback — a negative commission deducted from the partner's next payout.

Open the **⋮** menu next to **Create commission** and select **Create clawback**. You can also create a clawback from the partner profile: **⋮** → **Create commission refund** — the partner is preselected.

In the **Create clawback** sheet, set:

- **Partner** — the partner the amount is withheld from;
- **Amount** — the clawback amount;
- **Reason** — order canceled, fraud, terms violation, tracking error, payment failed, ineligible partner, duplicate commission, or other.

Click **Create clawback** — it appears in the commissions table as a negative commission.

pages.title: Configuring partner rewards
pages.description: Learn how to create custom rewards (pay-per-click, pay-per-lead, pay-per-sale) tailored to each partner with RevRoute Partners.

headings.text: Updating a partner group's reward configuration

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

On RevRoute Partners, you can offer different incentives for your partners to incentivize them to create high-quality content to spread the word about your product:

| Reward type                 | Description                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Click-based (pay-per-click) | Rewarding partners for driving clicks to your product – similar to how Google Ads' pay-per-click works.                                            |
| Lead-based (pay-per-lead)   | A more effective alternative to pay-per-click, where you reward partners for leads generated (e.g. demo requests, free trial signups, etc.)        |
| Sale-based (pay-per-sale)   | This is the most common reward type, where you reward partners for driving sales to your product either via a rev-share or fixed-price commission. |

During the program onboarding flow, you'll be asked to create a default group reward that will be automatically applied to all new partners who join your program.

This initial reward will be either a lead or a sale-based reward by default, but you can customize the reward terms accordingly.

## Default group rewards

After initial onboarding, you can create additional rewards for clicks, leads, or sales, depending on how you initially set up the group. These rewards will be made available to all partners who join your program.

## Creating a reward

Our reward builder lets you create simple and complex rewards quickly and easily. When the reward builder initially opens, you'll see the basics required to create a reward. Clicking on the different `Blue` and `Orange` input prompts allow you to change the structure of the reward.

### Configuring reward types

Depending on the type of reward you're creating, you can choose between a flat fee or a percentage-based commission:

| Reward Type | Model      | Description                                            | Example           |
| ----------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------- |
| **Click**   | Flat       | Partners receive a fixed fee for each click generated  | ₽200 per click    |
| **Lead**    | Flat       | Partners receive a fixed fee for each qualified lead   | ₽5,000 per lead   |
| **Sale**    | Percentage | Partners receive a percentage of sales (revenue share) | 30% of sale value |
| **Sale**    | Flat       | Partners receive a fixed fee for each completed sale   | ₽5,000 per sale   |

For sale rewards, you can further customize the recurring nature of the commission:

- One time
- For 3, 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, or 48 months
- For the customer's lifetime

### Adding reward conditions

**Совет.**

  Customizing reward conditions is only available on the Advanced plan and
  above.

On RevRoute, you can also set specific requirements for reward completion and can even reward a different type (flat rate or percentage), amount, and duration when they are met. For example, you can set conditions like the following:

- Higher rewards for sales and leads from a specific country
- Higher rewards for sales of specific products
- Higher rewards for partners with more than 100 conversions
- Higher rewards for sales over a specific amount

Click **Add condition** to set these parameters.

Each condition can be based on either `Customer`, `Sale`, or `Partner`, allowing you to mix and match reward conditions to suit your program best.

Conditions let you use `AND` or `OR` statements to control how they work. Each condition is tied only to its own reward and doesn't affect others. Your conditions can be as simple or as complex as you need.

### Custom reward descriptions

By default, RevRoute automatically generates reward descriptions when rewards are created. In some cases, you may want to customize how those rewards are presented to partners, whether that’s to better match your brand voice or to make a complex reward easier to understand.
To edit a reward’s content, click the **pencil icon** next to the main reward builder. This opens the content editor, where you can update the primary reward description and optionally add more context using the reward tooltip.

Click the description text to update the main description.

Click `Reward tooltip` to edit the tooltip content. Tooltips support basic markdown and allow up to 2,000 characters, making them ideal for adding detailed explanations or terms.

You can customize each field independently. For example, you might only update the tooltip for a more complex reward while leaving the main description unchanged. You can also do the opposite, updating the description without touching the tooltip. This flexibility lets you tailor each reward without extra work.

If you want to remove your custom content, click the **X** icon next to the custom description. The reward will revert to RevRoute’s default description.

### Reward preview

During the creation of your rewards, the reward preview will populate with the settings you've provided. This preview allows you to see exactly what your partner will see on your program details and within their dashboard. You can see it in the screenshots above.

## Reward examples

Here are a few reward examples with their conditions to give you some starting ideas.

**Совет.**

  Customizing reward conditions is only available on the Advanced plan and
  above.

### Geo-specific

Tailor your reward amount by customer country. In this example, we're rewarding partners with a higher percentage for conversions from Russia and Kazakhstan:

| Condition                                                   | Reward                                    | Description                                 |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| If `Customer` `Country` `is one of` `Russia, Kazakhstan`     | Then pay a `Percentage` of `30%` per sale | Higher reward for customers from Russia and Kazakhstan |
| If `Customer` `Country` `is not one of` `Russia, Kazakhstan` | Then pay a `Percentage` of `10%` per sale | Lower reward for other customers            |

### Product spotlight

Tailor your reward amount by product. In this example, we're rewarding more when the sale is for the Gold Plan:

| Condition                                  | Reward                                    | Description                           |
| ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| If`Sale` `Product ID` `is` `prod_xxx`      | Then pay a `Percentage` of `40%` per sale | Higher reward for `prod_xxx` sales    |
| If `Sale` `Product ID` `is not` `prod_xxx` | Then pay a `Percentage` of `10%` per sale | Lower reward for non-`prod_xxx` sales |

**Справка.**

  Where `prod_xxx` is listed, you'll enter your product ID.

If you forward sale events from your billing system, the product ID is the
product/plan identifier from that system (e.g. a SKU or plan code).

If you're manually tracking a sale event via our `/track/sale` endpoint, you
can pass along the product ID via the metadata
prop
(e.g. `metadata.productId = "prod_xxx"`).

### Partner performance tiers

Tailor your reward amount by partner performance. In this example, we offer a 25% base reward and increase it to 35% for partners with 200 or more conversions:

| Condition                                                               | Reward                                    | Description                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| If `Partner` `Total conversions` `is greater than or equal to` `200`      | Then pay a `Percentage` of `35%` per sale | Higher reward for partners with 200+ conversions                        |
| If `Partner` `Total revenue` `is greater than or equal to` `₽1,000,000`   | Then pay a `Percentage` of `35%` per sale | Higher reward for partners with ₽1M+ in referral revenue                |
| If `Partner` `Total commissions` `is greater than or equal to` `₽100,000` | Then pay a `Percentage` of `35%` per sale | Higher reward for partners who have earned ₽100,000+ in commissions     |

**Совет.**

  Want to move partners to a different partner group based on their performance
  instead? Learn more about group move
  rules.

### Staggered reward durations

Tailor your reward amount by how long the customer has been subscribed, using the `Customer` → `Subscription duration` condition (in months).

In this example, we're offering a 25% reward for the first 12 months and a 10% reward for all other sales:

| Condition                                                                 | Reward                                    | Description                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| If `Customer` `Subscription duration` `is less than or equal to` `12 mo.` | Then pay a `Percentage` of `25%` per sale | Higher reward in the first year |
| Group's main reward                                                       | `Percentage` of `10%` per sale, lifetime  | For all other sales             |

### Sale amount modifiers

For creating tiered rewards based on the sale amount. In this example, we're giving our partners a higher reward if the sale amount is over a specific amount:

| Condition                                               | Reward                                    | Description                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| If `Sale` `Amount` `is greater than or equal to` `₽10,000` | Then pay a `Percentage` of `40%` per sale | Higher reward for sales of ₽10,000+  |
| If `Sale` `Amount` `is less than` `₽10,000`                | Then pay a `Percentage` of `20%` per sale | Lower reward for sales under ₽10,000 |

## Updating a partner group's reward configuration

You can update a partner group's reward configuration at any time. When this happens, historical commissions won't be updated.

However, the reward configuration for a partner-customer pair will be updated. E.g., if a partner used to be on a one-time reward and was switched to recurring rewards, all subsequent subscription renewals from their **previous referrals** will be eligible for commission again.

To avoid this, instead of editing a given partner group's reward configuration directly, create separate partner groups for one-time vs recurring rewards. This way, when you move partners from one group to the other, the reward configuration for the partner's previous referrals will be preserved.

### Group reward update logs

For transparency and auditability, we also keep a history of all reward updates for a given group:

This helps you track changes over time and understand the impact of your reward configurations on the generated partner commissions.

pages.title: Topping up the partner payout balance
pages.description: Where RevRoute takes the money for partner payouts: your RocketWork account balance for self-employed partners and sole proprietors, the nominal account at T-Bank for legal entities. How to top up and what to do if the balance is too low.

headings.text: If no payout channel is connected
How to top up the balance
If the balance is too low

pages.body:
**Совет.**

  Partner payouts are available on the Business plan and above.

RevRoute sends partner payouts from balances that you top up in advance with a transfer from your
company account: the payouts you confirm
are paid from these balances. The card you use to pay for your RevRoute subscription is not involved
in payouts.

## Where payouts are paid from

The balance depends on the partner's tax status:

| Partner | Where the money comes from | Where to see the balance |
|---|---|---|
| **Self-employed, sole proprietor** | Your company's RocketWork account balance | The **RocketWork account** card on the **Payouts** page |
| **Legal entity** | Your balance on the RevRoute nominal account at T-Bank | The **Nominal account — legal entities** card on the **Payouts** page |

Individuals without a tax status can't be paid through RevRoute.

To see which channels your program has, open **Payouts** → **Payout settings** → the **Payout
method** block: connected channels are marked **Connected**.

## If no payout channel is connected

In that case the **Payout method** block says **No payout methods**, and the payout confirmation
window says **Payouts through RevRoute aren't connected**. To connect:

1. Open **Settings → Billing**.
2. Fill in the **Company details** block.
3. To pay legal entity partners, tick **I accept the terms of the agency agreement (Document No. 3)**.
4. Click **Save**.

If you've accepted Document No. 3, the nominal account is connected automatically after saving: the
form shows the bank's check of your company, then **Nominal account connected**.

The RocketWork account for paying self-employed partners and sole proprietors is opened by the RevRoute
team using your company details — you don't need to register with RocketWork or the bank yourself. To
speed things up, contact RevRoute support after saving your details. Once the account is open, the
**Payout method** block shows **RocketWork** marked **Connected**.

If you pay partners yourself outside RevRoute, you don't need a balance — choose the **Manual**
payout method (learn more).

## How to top up the balance

1. Open **Payouts** in the program menu.
2. On the **RocketWork account** or **Nominal account — legal entities** card, click **Top-up
   details**.
3. Click **Copy details** and transfer the money from your company account. For the nominal account,
   use the payment purpose exactly as shown — the payer's TIN links the transfer to your account
   automatically.
4. Wait for the balance on the card to update. The nominal account balance refreshes every 10
   minutes.

Step-by-step guides with screenshots: Payout via RocketWork
and Legal entity payout.

## How much you need

The **Confirm payouts** window shows the totals for each invoice:

- **RocketWork** — the **RocketWork funding budget** line. Also allow for the RocketWork commission:
  it is debited from the same balance according to your plan.
- **Nominal account** — the **Legal entities receive** and **Fee (legal entities)** lines added
  together: payouts to legal entities plus the 5% RevRoute fee.

If the invoice includes partners of both types, you need money on both balances.

## If the balance is too low

**When confirming.** While the balance is too low, the confirm button in the **Confirm payouts**
window is disabled, and a **Top up** link appears next to the balance.

1. Top up the balance that is short (see above).
2. Wait for it to update on the card.
3. Click **Confirm payouts** again.

If only one balance is short, you can exclude that channel's partners from the invoice with the
**Exclude** button in their rows and confirm the rest.

**After confirming.** Before paying a RocketWork task, RevRoute checks the RocketWork account balance
against the partner amount and the task commission once more. If the balance is short, the payout
stays **Processing** and is sent automatically once you top up the account.

## Related topics

- Sending partner payouts
- Payout via RocketWork
- Legal entity payout
- Receiving payouts as a partner

pages.title: How to pay a legal entity partner through the nominal account
pages.description: Step by step for program owners: create a commission for a company partner, top up RevRoute's nominal account at T-Bank, confirm the payout and track its status.
pages.body:
Programs pay company partners to their settlement account through RevRoute's nominal account at
T-Bank. No contracts or receipts per payout: the money comes from your balance on the nominal account
and the bank transfers it to the company's account. From you — a commission, enough balance and the
payout confirmation.

By now the partner has set the Legal entity status and bank details, and the bank has checked the
company — the partner shows **Ready** (see the partner's side in
Legal entity payouts). You can
check readiness yourself too: the partner card has a **Payout readiness** line, and the partner list
shows a tooltip on the partner's icon.

## Create a commission

Commissions usually appear on their own — from sales through the partner's links. A one-off payout
(bonus, reimbursement) can be created manually.

### 1. Create commission

Open **Commissions** in the program menu and click **Create commission** (or press `C`).

### 2. Partner

Pick the company partner from the list — start typing its name.

### 3. One-off type

**One-off** — a bonus or reimbursement not tied to a sale. It is available for payout right away: the
holding period doesn't apply.

### 4. Amount

Enter the amount in rubles. The description is optional — the partner sees it.

### 5. Create commission

Click **Create commission**. The commission appears in the list, and **Payouts** shows a pending payout
to the partner.

## Check the nominal account balance

### 6. Balance and top-up details

Open **Payouts**. At the top is the **Nominal account — legal entities** card with your balance. If it
doesn't cover the pending payouts, click **Top-up details** and transfer money from your company
account. Incoming transfers are matched automatically; the balance refreshes every 10 minutes.

### 7. Confirm payouts

The **Pending payouts** card shows the amount ready for payout and, below it, the program's minimum
payout. Amounts below the minimum accumulate until the next period; change the threshold with the
**Change** link. Click **Confirm payouts**.

## Confirm the payout

### 8. Check the totals

The **Confirm payouts** window shows where the money comes from and how much the company receives:

| Line | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Amount** | Commissions earned by partners for the period |
| **Legal entities receive** | What arrives to the companies' settlement accounts |
| **Fee (legal entities)** | RevRoute's 5 % fee on payouts to legal entities |
| **Total** | The amount of the whole invoice |

Your nominal account balance is debited by the **Legal entities receive** and **Fee (legal
entities)** lines added together. If the invoice also has self-employed partners or sole
proprietors, RocketWork lines appear next to these.

### 9. Press and hold

Press and hold the button at the bottom of the window until it fills up. While the balance is short,
the button is disabled — top up the nominal account (step 6) and come back.

## Transfer and statuses

### 10. RevRoute approves the payout

After confirmation you see **Payout confirmed**. The payout gets the **Processing** status: RevRoute
reviews and approves it, then the bank creates a deal on the nominal account and transfers the money.
The partner receives a payout email.

### 11. Statuses on the Payouts page

After approval the payout becomes **Sent**, and once the money reaches the company's account —
**Completed**, with the date in the **Paid** column. The nominal account balance decreases by the total
from step 8.

General rules — minimum amount, holding period, payout statuses — are in
Sending partner payouts. Self-employed
partners and sole proprietors are paid through RocketWork — Payout via RocketWork.

pages.title: Sending partner payouts on RevRoute
pages.description: Partner payouts on RevRoute: RocketWork for self-employed partners and sole proprietors, the nominal account for legal entities, manual payouts, statuses, holding period, minimum amount and one-click confirmation.
pages.body:
**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Business plans and
  above.

RevRoute Partners pays partners in one click: you top up the payout balance and confirm the invoice,
and RevRoute sends each payout through RocketWork or the nominal account at T-Bank, prepares
documents for your accounting and shows the status of every payout.

If you're running a program with hundreds of partners, you don't need to transfer money to each of
them separately or track failures by hand.

## Supported payout methods

The payout channel depends on the tax status the partner sets in their
payout settings:

| Partner | How RevRoute pays | Where the money comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Self-employed** | Through RocketWork: a one-off contract for each payout, which the partner signs with an SMS code; the NPD receipt is generated automatically. The money goes where the partner chose in the RocketWork X app: a card, SBP or an account. | Your company's RocketWork account balance |
| **Sole proprietor** | Through RocketWork: a one-off contract for each payout, signed with an SMS code; the money goes to the sole proprietor's settlement account. | Your company's RocketWork account balance |
| **Legal entity** | From the RevRoute nominal account at T-Bank to the company's settlement account. No contracts or receipts per payout. | Your balance on the nominal account |

Individuals without a tax status can't be paid through RevRoute.

To see which channels your program has, open **Payout settings** → the **Payout method** block:
**RocketWork** and **T-Bank nominal account** are marked **Connected**. If there are none, fill in
**Company details** under **Settings → Billing** — see
Topping up the payout balance.

Step by step for each channel:

- Payout via RocketWork — self-employed partners and sole proprietors;
- Legal entity payout — through the nominal account.

**Примечание.**

  Payouts are sent in **RUB**.

## Paying partners yourself

If you pay a partner yourself, outside RevRoute, choose the **Manual** payout method:

- for the whole program — **Payout settings** → **Default payout channel** → **Manual**;
- for a single partner — on the partner's page.

These payouts carry a **Manual** badge in the table. Once you've paid the partner, select the payouts
in the table and click **Mark as paid**. The partner doesn't need a tax status or a RocketWork or
nominal account connection for this, and RevRoute charges no fee on these payouts.

## Tax handling

Partners pay their own taxes:

- **Self-employed (NPD regime)** — RocketWork issues the NPD receipt for each payout; the partner
  doesn't need to issue it in the Moy Nalog ("My Tax") app. Tax: 4% on payments from individuals, 6%
  on payments from businesses.
- **Sole proprietor (IP)** — declares the income under their own tax regime.
- **Legal entity** — declares the income under its own tax regime.

**Внимание.**

  RevRoute does not withhold or remit taxes on the partner's behalf. You can see whether a partner is
  ready for payouts on their page — the **Payout readiness** row.

## Payouts dashboard

To view your payouts, go to your **Partner Program** tab and click on the **Payouts** page.

At the top of the page, you'll see your balance cards (**RocketWork account**, **Nominal account — legal entities**) with a **Top-up details** button, and a summary of your pending and completed payouts:

**Pending payouts**

This shows the total amount of commissions that are eligible for payment.

Hovering over the total will show you:

- **Eligible payouts** – due commissions that have reached the minimum amount, for partners who have connected payouts.
- **Ineligible payouts** – the rest: the partner hasn't connected payouts yet (no tax status, or RocketWork or the bank hasn't confirmed their details), or the amount is below the minimum.

Once you have at least one pending payout on RevRoute, you can click the **Confirm payouts** button to review and confirm them.

**Total paid**

This shows the total amount of all commissions you've paid out to your partners.

Hovering over the total will show you:

- **Completed payouts** — payouts that RocketWork or the bank has carried through to the end
- **Processing payouts** — payouts that are still in progress

Click **View invoices** to access past payout invoices.

In the payout table below, you can track and manage your payouts, confirm pending ones, and review past activity.

| Column  | Description                                                                                                                 |
| ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Period  | The payout range, starting from the date of the partner's first commission to the end of the month of their last commission |
| Partner | The partner receiving the payout                                                                                            |
| Status  | The current payout status                       |
| Paid    | The date the payout was confirmed, and by whom                                                                              |
| Amount  | The total amount paid to the partner                                                                                        |

## Payout statuses

A payout can have one of the following statuses:

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Pending | The payout hasn't been confirmed yet: it's waiting for your confirmation, for the partner to connect payouts, or for the amount to reach the minimum. |
| Processing | The payout was confirmed and RevRoute is setting it up with the provider: in RocketWork, a one-off contract waiting for the partner's signature; on the nominal account, RevRoute's approval and a bank transaction. |
| Sent | RocketWork or the bank is transferring the money to the partner. |
| Completed | The money has reached the partner. |
| Failed | The provider didn't carry out the payout. Contact RevRoute support — the payout will be reconciled with the provider. |
| Canceled | The payout was canceled — for example, when a partner is banned from the program. |

**Совет.**

  Statuses are updated automatically from RocketWork and bank data.
  There's nothing for you to do.

## Payout holding period

On RevRoute, you can also set a "payout holding period" to specify how long your commissions will be held in "pending" status before becoming eligible for payout.

This is useful for safeguarding against potential refunds, chargebacks, or fraudulent transactions.

**Справка.**

  If a sale tracked via your billing system is refunded, RevRoute will mark the corresponding commission as
  refunded
  — provided you've passed `invoiceId` when tracking the original sale.

To set a payout holding period for your program, go to your individual groups and click on the **Settings** tab. Here you'll find the payout holding period settings in the "Additional settings" group.

Your options include the following:

- 0 days (default)
- 7 days
- 14 days
- 30 days
- 60 days
- 90 days

When you update the payout holding period, you can apply the new setting to every group at once. Just select the box labelled `Apply to all groups` before confirming. The change will take effect right away.

## Minimum payout amount

You can also set an optional "minimum payout amount" (e.g. 1 000 ₽). When this is set, partners with earnings below the minimum payout amount won't be eligible for payout until they reach the specific threshold set.

Click the button in the top right to show the **Payout settings**. Unlike the payout holding period, this setting is program-wide.

## How to pay your partners

When one or more of your partners have earned more than the minimum payout amount, click **Confirm payouts** from the payouts dashboard to open the payout details.

- **Method:** where the money comes from — **RocketWork balance** and/or **Nominal account balance**, with the current balance. If it's too low, a **Top up** link appears next to it — see Topping up the payout balance.
- **Cutoff Period:** If set, only commissions earned on or before this date will be paid. Useful for reconciliation payouts for a specific fiscal period (e.g. last month, last quarter) without including newer commissions.
- **Partners**, **Amount**, **RevRoute fee**, the amounts per channel and **Total** — the invoice summary. What each line means is explained in Payout via RocketWork and Legal entity payout.

If everything looks right, press and hold the button at the bottom of the window until the payout is confirmed. While the balance is too low, the button is disabled.

After confirmation, RevRoute sets up each payout with the provider separately: for self-employed partners and sole proprietors, a one-off contract in RocketWork that the partner signs with an SMS code; for legal entities, a nominal account transaction after RevRoute's approval. You can follow each payout by its status.

### Excluding payouts

In some cases, you may want to exclude a partner's payout from the current batch. To do this, hover over the partner's row in the payouts table and click **Exclude**. This removes the partner from the current payout batch.

If you need to add the partner back, hover over their row and click **Include**. This adds them back to the current payout batch.

## Payout fees and timing

- **RevRoute fee** — 5% of payouts made through RevRoute. The amount for each invoice is shown in the **Confirm payouts** window. Payouts you make manually carry no fee.
- **RocketWork commission** is debited from your RocketWork account balance according to your plan.
- **Nominal account** — the amount is sent to the bank in whole rubles.

Self-employed partners and sole proprietors get the money only after they sign the contract in RocketWork. Legal entities — after RevRoute approves the payout.

## Topping up the payout balance

To pay partners through RevRoute, top up your RocketWork account balance (for self-employed partners and sole proprietors) and/or the nominal account (for legal entities) in advance with a transfer from your company account. The details are on the **Payouts** page — the **Top-up details** button on the balance card.

RevRoute checks the balance when you confirm payouts and won't let you confirm the invoice if it's too low. Learn more in Topping up the payout balance.

pages.title: How to pay a partner through RocketWork
pages.description: Step by step for a vendor: create a commission, top up the RocketWork balance and confirm the payout to self-employed partners and sole proprietors.
pages.body:
Programs pay self-employed partners and sole proprietors through RocketWork: money leaves your
company's RocketWork balance, a one-off contract is issued for each payout, and the self-employed
partner's NPD receipt is generated automatically. You need an earned commission, enough balance and a
payout confirmation.

By now the partner has set the tax status and connected RocketWork — their status is **Ready** (see
the self-employed and
sole proprietor guides).

## Create a commission

Commissions usually appear on their own from sales through partner links. A one-off payout (bonus,
reimbursement) can be added manually.

### 1. Create commission

Open **Commissions** in the program menu and click **Create commission** (or press `C`).

### 2. Partner

Pick the partner from the list — start typing the name.

### 3. One-time type

**One-time** — a bonus or reimbursement not tied to a sale. It is payable immediately: the holding
period doesn't apply.

### 4. Amount

Enter the amount in rubles. The description is optional and visible to the partner.

### 5. Save

Click **Create commission**. It appears in the list, and a pending payout to the partner appears in
**Payouts**.

## Check the RocketWork balance

### 6. Balance and top-up details

Open **Payouts**. At the top is the **RocketWork account** card with the current balance. If it
doesn't cover pending payouts, click **Top-up details** and transfer money from the company account.
Mind RocketWork's fee: it is charged from the same balance at your rate.

### 7. Confirm payouts

The **Pending payouts** card shows the amount ready to pay. Click **Confirm payouts**.

## Confirm the payout

### 8. Check the totals

The **Confirm payouts** window shows where the money comes from and what each partner gets:

| Row | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Amount** | Commissions earned by partners for the period |
| **RevRoute fee** | 5 % of payouts made through RevRoute |
| **Partners receive** | What partners receive after the fee |
| **RocketWork funding budget** | What is charged to the RocketWork balance |
| **Legal entities receive** | Payouts to companies via the nominal account, if any |

### 9. Press and hold

Press and hold the button at the bottom. While the balance is insufficient the button is disabled —
top up (step 6) and come back.

## Partner signature and transfer

### 10. Payout confirmed

After holding the button you see **Payout confirmed** with the amount and number of partners.
The money is charged to the RocketWork balance, and RevRoute creates a one-off contract in RocketWork
for each payout. **View invoices** opens the invoice for this payout.

### 11. Statuses in Payouts

The partner gets an email and signs the contract with an SMS code. After signing RocketWork transfers
the money: the payout becomes **Sent**, then **Completed**. The RocketWork balance decreases by the
amount paid to the partner plus RocketWork's fee.

General rules — minimum amount, holding period, payout statuses — are in
Sending partner payouts.

pages.title: How noindex works on RevRoute
pages.description: Learn how RevRoute supports noindex response headers for short links with custom domains.

headings.text: How to index your short links on Google

pages.body:
If you're familiar with SEO best practices, you might have heard of the `noindex` meta tag that tells search engines not to index a page.

This is particularly important if you're using RevRoute with a custom domain – specifically a subdomain – for your short links, since having them indexed could potentially have a negative impact on your SEO.

To prevent this, RevRoute automatically serves short links with a `noindex` response header when you're using a custom domain. This tells search engines not to index your short links, keeping them out of search results.

The `/noindex` and `/doindex` keys in the examples below are placeholder short link keys, and `go.acme-demo.ru` is an example custom domain.

[пример кода: bash]

**Справка.**

  If you're using RevRoute with the default `link.revroute.ru` domain, the
  `noindex` response header is **_not applied by default_**.

## How to index your short links on Google

If you would like your short links to be indexed anyway, you can easily enable indexing by following these steps:

1. Go to your RevRoute dashboard.
2. Click on the `⋮` button of the link that you want to enable indexing for, which will open the dropdown menu.
3. In the dropdown menu, click on the **Edit** button, which will open the RevRoute link builder.
4. Click on the `...` button, which will open the dropdown menu.
5. In the dropdown menu, click on the **Add Search Engine Indexing** button to enable indexing.

And that's it! Your link will now be served without the `noindex` response header:

[пример кода: bash]

**Совет.**

  This feature is only available on Pro plans and
  above.

pages.title: How can I check a RevRoute link's destination before clicking on it?
pages.description: Learn how to check a RevRoute link's destination to make sure it's safe to click on.
pages.body:
If you're not sure where a RevRoute link will take you, you can check its destination before clicking on it by adding a `+` sign to the end of the short link.

For example, if you want to check the destination of the short link `link.revroute.ru/sale26`, you can type `link.revroute.ru/sale26+` into your browser's address bar and press `Enter`.

This will take you to the link inspector page, which shows you the destination URL of the short link, as well as the respective social media preview for the URL.

## Reporting a malicious link

If you suspect that a RevRoute link is malicious, click the flag icon on the link inspector page to report it. We take these reports seriously and will take appropriate action as soon as possible.

Learn more about the types of links that are against our Terms of Service.

pages.title: How to export links from RevRoute
pages.description: Learn more about how to export your links from your RevRoute workspace to a CSV file.
pages.body:
In your RevRoute workspace, you can export your links to a CSV file. This is useful if you want to analyze the data locally or share them with an external stakeholder.

To export your links, follow these steps:

**Open the Export links modal**

    In your RevRoute workspace, navigate to the **Links** page.

    Then, click on the `⋮` button next to the search bar to open the more options dropdown menu. Select **Export links** → **Export to CSV**.

**Select the date range**

    In the **Export links** modal, choose the **Date Range** for the links you want to export. By default, **All Time** is selected — RevRoute will export all links.

**Select the columns to export**

    RevRoute will export the following columns by default:
    - Short link
    - Destination URL
    - Clicks
    - Created at

pages.title: How to transfer links between workspaces?
pages.description: Learn how to transfer your RevRoute default short links from one workspace to another.

headings.text: Step 1: Open the link transfer modal

pages.body:
Transferring links between workspaces is a common use case for many RevRoute users, especially when they want to reorganize their links or consolidate them into a single workspace.

This guide will show you how to transfer your RevRoute short links from one workspace to another.

**Внимание.**

  Transferring a link will also **fully reset its stats** and is irreversible
  – please proceed with caution.

## Step 1: Open the link transfer modal

For a given link, click on the `⋮` button and select **Transfer**.

You can also use the `T` keyboard shortcut to open the transfer modal.

## Step 2: Select the destination workspace

In the **Transfer link** modal, use the **Select workspace** selector to pick the workspace you want to transfer the link to:

To verify, type `confirm transfer link` in the confirmation field and click **Transfer link** to complete the transfer.

That's it! Your link should now be successfully transferred to the new workspace.

## Caveats

- Transferring a link will also **fully reset its stats** and is irreversible – please proceed with caution.
- You can only transfer links on the default RevRoute domain (`link.revroute.ru`) between workspaces. If you want to transfer a custom domain link, you'll need to transfer the domain itself to the new workspace.
- Link tags are not transferred when you transfer a link between workspaces. You'll need to re-apply the tags to the link in the new workspace.
- You can only transfer links to workspaces that you have access to. If you don't have access to the destination workspace, you won't be able to transfer the link.
